When the subject is what the action is directed at, then the sentence is said to be in passive form/voice. For example: Active Voice: Rita and her friends performed a skit. Here 'Rita and her friends' (subject) perform the action. Passive Voice: A skit was performed by Rita and her friends. Here 'skit' is the subject (at which the action is directed).

t:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. 
She always tried to help others in need, as she is good and wisest, and she knew how to do it in the most effective way possible.
o: She always tried to help others in need,
as she knew how to do it in the
is good and wisest, and she
e:
Coordinating conjunctions join items that are of equal importance in a sentence. Also, it joins two words of equal grammatical rank.
Here, 'good' is a positive adjective and 'wiser' is a comparative adjective so they cannot be placed together.
The correct sentence is - She always tried to help others in need, as she is good and wise, and she knew how to do it in the most effective way possible.
Hence, option (d) is correct.

t:
Identify the error in the given sentence and select the correct sentence from the given options.
Petrified wood is type of fossilised wood that exhibits the original details of the wood.
o: Petrified wood is the type of fossilised wood that exhibits a original details of the wood.
A petrified wood is type of fossilised wood that exhibits an original details of the wood.
The petrified wood is the type of fossilised wood that exhibits a original details of the wood.
Petrified wood is a type of fossilised wood that exhibits the original details of the wood.
e:
· Original sentence: "Petrified wood is type of fossilised wood that exhibits the original details of the wood."
· Error: Missing article "a" before "type," making it grammatically incomplete ("is type" should be "is a type").
· Option 1: "Petrified wood is the type.. a original details" - Incorrect; "a original" should be "the original" (article mismatch).
· Option 2: "A petrified wood is type.. an original details" - Incorrect; "a petrified wood" is wrong (no article needed before "petrified wood" as a general noun), and "an original details" is ungrammatical ("details" is plural, needs "the original").
· Option 3: "The petrified wood is the type.. a original details" - Incorrect; "the petrified wood" implies a specific piece (not general), and "a original details" is wrong.
· Option 4: "Petrified wood is a type of fossilised wood that exhibits the original details of the wood" - Correct; adds "a" before "type" and uses "the original details" appropriately for a general statement.
Thus, option 4 is the correct sentence.

t: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
o: They have know each other since childhood.
Arnav has lived in this city for ten years.
We have just move into our new house.
They had buy tickets for the concert, but it was cancelled at the last minute.
e: The sentence given in option (b) is grammatically correct. Option (a) is not correct. In the present perfect tense (indicated by the helping verb 'have'), the correct form of the main verb after "have" is the past participle form. But 'know' (base form) is not the past participle form of the verb. Accordingly, 'know' should be replaced with the past participle form 'known'. The correct sentence is: They have known each other since childhood. Option (c) is incorrect. In the present perfect tense (indicated by the helping verb 'have'), the correct form of the main verb after "have" is the past participle form. But 'move' (base form) is not the past participle form of the verb. Accordingly, 'move' should be replaced with the past participle form 'moved'. The correct sentence is: We have just moved into our new house. Option (d) is also incorrect. In the past perfect tense (indicated by the helping verb 'had'), the correct form of the main verb after "had" is the past participle form. But the verb "buy" (base form) is not the past participle form of the verb. Accordingly, 'buy' should be replaced with the past participle form 'bought'. Also, "had bought" is used to indicate an action that occurred before another action in the past (in this case, the cancellation of the concert). The correct sentence is: They had bought tickets for the concert, but it was cancelled at the last minute. Hence, (b) is the correct answer. NOTE: Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English, participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below: Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground. Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion. The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect. The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes the completed action or state of the thing spoken of. A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n. One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and a present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.

t:
In the following question, a sentence is given with an underlined phrase. Select the option given below that can replace the phrase to make the sentence grammatically and contextually correct and mark that as your answer. 
How <u>many milk does</u> a baby need in the first few days?
e: 'Many' and 'few' are followed by a plural countable noun. 'Milk' is an uncountable noun so the use of uncountable quantifier 'much' is appropriate here followed by verb in singular form as 'a baby' is a singular noun. Hence, option (b) is correct. NOTE/- Countable and uncountable nouns: 1. Countable nouns are the class of nouns that can be counted, for example, 'table' - one table, two tables, three tables, etc. 2. Uncountable nouns are the nouns that cannot be counted or usually are not counted, for example, light, water, milk, information, furniture, etc. They do not generally have a plural form and can't be preceded by 'a' or 'an'. Many abstract nouns are typically uncountable. Some uncountable nouns can be used in the plural as well, depending on the meaning or context of the word.

t:
Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
<u>My elder brother</u>, who is <u>a renowned architect</u>, <u>often gives me</u> <u>valuable advices regarding</u> career choices and professional development.
e: The error is in the segment "valuable advices regarding". The noun "advice" is an uncountable noun, meaning it does not typically have a plural form "advices". To refer to multiple pieces of advice, one might say "pieces of advice" or simply use "advice" as it encompasses the general concept. Correct sentence: My elder brother, who is a renowned architect, often gives me valuable advice regarding career choices and professional development. Hence, option (d) is the correct answer. Note: · Countable and uncountable nouns: 1. Countable nouns are the class of nouns that can be counted, for example, 'table' - one table, two tables, three tables, etc. 2. Uncountable nouns are the nouns that cannot be counted or usually are not counted, for example, light, water, milk, information, furniture, etc. They do not generally have a plural form and can't be preceded by 'a' or 'an'. Many abstract nouns are typically uncountable. Some uncountable nouns can be used in the plural as well, depending on the meaning or context of the word.

t:
Select the grammatically correct sentence.

A. He do not like spicy food.
B. He were not like spicy food.
C. He are not like spicy food.
D. He doesn't like spicy food.
e:
The subject "he" is singular, so it requires a singular verb form [does]. 'Do', 'were' and 'are' are plural helping verbs, so they can't be used. Therefore, the correct sentence is "He doesn't like spicy food."
Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

t:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.
Me and my colleague have decided / to take up the challenging new project / offered by the senior management team.
o: Me and my colleague have decided
to take up the challenging new project
offered by the senior management team
e: The error is in the part "Me and my colleague have decided". When a pronoun is part of a compound subject (performing the action of the verb "have decided"), the subjective case of the pronoun should be used. "Me" is an objective pronoun. The correct subjective pronoun is "I". Also, it is conventional to place the pronoun "I" after other nouns or pronouns in a compound subject. Correct Sentence: My colleague and I have decided to take up the challenging new project offered by the senior management team. Hence, option (a) is the correct answer. Note: · Subjective Pronouns: The pronouns I, you, we, he, she, it, and they are known as subjective pronouns because they act as the subjects of verbs: We went to the party. "I" is the correct subjective pronoun here. · Objective Pronouns: The pronouns me, you, us, him, her, it, and them are called objective pronouns because they act as the objects of verbs and prepositions. "Me" is incorrectly used as a subject.

t:
The
following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the
segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: Radha bought a sheet of paper
e:
Replace Stationary with Stationery.
"Stationary" and "Stationery" are two words that are often confused with each other due to their similar spellings, but they have very different meanings:


Stationary (adjective):- Means not moving or remaining in one place. Examples:


- The car is stationary.
 - The bike is stationary on the rack.


Stationery (noun): Refers to writing and office supplies, such as paper, pens, pencils, and envelopes. Examples:


- I need to buy some stationery for my office.
 - The store sells a variety of stationery items.
To help you remember the difference:


If you can replace the word with "not moving", use "stationary".


If you're talking about office supplies, use "stationery".

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: The bilingual guide asserted that English and Hindi are relatively easy
languages, but he was disappointed to find that the new intern
could not speak both of them fluently during the orientation.
e: The Correct Ans is Option (C).Replace “could not speak both” with “could speak neither”.📌 Rule / Concept: "Both" in Negative SentencesThe word both is used to emphasize the inclusion of two people or things in an affirmative (positive) statement. However, both should never be used with a negative verb (not) to mean "none of the two."When you want to say "not the first one AND not the second one," the correct construction is to use neither with a positive verb. Using "both... not" is considered a grammatical error in competitive exams because it creates logical ambiguity.Incorrect UsageWrong example 1: Both of them are not going to the party. ❌Wrong example 2: I do not have both the books you asked for. ❌More Examples for Clarity - Example 1: Neither of the two brothers is honest. ✅ (Instead of: Both brothers are not honest.)Example 2: I like neither tea nor coffee. ✅ (Instead of: I do not like both tea and coffee.)

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: The stern judge, known for his uncompromising nature,
felt a father in him surge with emotion when he saw
his long-lost daughter standing in the witness box.
e: Replace “a father” with “the father”.Rule / Concept: Common Noun used as an Abstract Noun –When a Common Noun (like father, mother, judge, patriot) is used to express a quality, an inner feeling, or an instinct rather than a specific physical person, it functions as an Abstract Noun. In this unique grammatical construction, the noun is always preceded by the definite article 'the'.Corrected Sentence- The stern judge, known for his uncompromising nature, felt the father in him surge with emotion when he saw his long-lost daughter standing in the witness box.More Examples for Clarity1. The mother in her could not see the child go hungry. (The motherly instinct)2. When he saw the enemy, the soldier in him awoke. (The bravery/spirit of a soldier)Things to Remember / Exam Tips-The "In him/her" Trigger: 90% of the time, this rule is tested using the structure: [The + Common Noun + in + him/her/them]. If you see this pattern, ensure "The" is present.The Meaning Shift: A mother = A woman. The mother (in her) = Motherly affection.

t:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
The decoration/ is being/ done grandly/ with Karthik.
e: The part given in option (b) has the error. The given sentence is in Passive voice in which the preposition 'by' is required to denote the doer of the action but in the sentence, 'with' is incorrectly used. The correct sentence is: The decoration is being done grandly by Karthik. Hence, the correct answer is option (b). Note: Active and Passive Voice: When the person doing the action is the subject, the sentence is said to be in active form/voice. When the subject is what the action is directed at, then the sentence is said to be in passive form/voice. For example: Active Voice: Rita and her friends performed a skit. Here 'Rita and her friends' (subject) perform the action. Passive Voice: A skit was performed by Rita and her friends. Here 'skit' is the subject (at which the action is directed). A Preposition is a word placed before a noun or a pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition) and shows a relationship in space or time or a logical relationship between two or more people, places, or things in a sentence. Examples I. The teacher scolded the child for being late. II. We're going to a party. · The words in bold are called prepositions because they normally take position before (pre) a noun/pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition. · The noun/pronoun which is used with a preposition is called its Object.

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: Despite his humble beginnings and lack of
him a Dhanwantari of their local community.
e: Replace “a” with “the”.Rule/Concept: Proper Nouns used as Metaphors (Comparison):Generally, Proper Nouns (names of persons, places, etc.) do not take an article. However, when a Proper Noun is used to represent a specific quality or to compare one person's traits to a famous personality, it acts as a Common Noun. In such cases, if we are comparing 'A' to 'B' to show 'A' is the best or a specific example of that quality in a particular group, we use the definite article 'The'.Application to the Given Question - Here, the person is being compared to "Dhanwantari" (the deity of medicine) to signify his healing skills within a specific group (the local community). When a person is hailed as the equivalent of a famous figure within a specific domain or location, 'The' is used to denote that specific status.

t:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.
She couldn't hardly believe / her eyes when she saw / the surprising news report.
e: The error is in the phrase "She couldn't hardly believe" due to a double negative. "Couldn't" (could not) is already negative. "Hardly" is a semi-negative adverb meaning "scarcely" or "almost not." Using both together creates a double negative, which is grammatically incorrect and can confuse the meaning. The sentence should express that she found it difficult to believe. The correct forms would be "She could hardly believe" or "She couldn't believe." Correct Sentence: She could hardly believe her eyes when she saw the surprising news report. (Or: She couldn't believe her eyes when she saw the surprising news report.) Hence, option (c) is the correct answer. Note: · Double Negative: A grammatical construction in which two negative words are used in the same clause to express a single negation. Standard English generally avoids double negatives.

t:
In the following sentence, the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.
The children were <u>merry</u> than usual on Sunday.
e: The comparative form of "merry" is "merrier," used with "than" for comparing two items. "More merrier" is redundant, and "the merriest" or "merriest" are superlatives, unsuitable for a two-item comparison. The complete sentence is: "The children were merrier than usual on Sunday."

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: The project manager will not authorize the
disbursement of funds unless the contractor
will submit the audited expenditure reports.
e: The Correct Ans is Option (C). Replace “will submit” with “submits”.📌 Rule/Concept: The "No Will" Rule in Conditional Clauses Don’t use future tense with these conjunctions- when, while, if, until, unless, provided that, as soon as, before, after, etc. Always write the condition part in simple future tense.In a Type 1 Conditional sentence (expressing a probable future), the sentence is divided into two parts: the Conditional Clause (starting with if, unless, until, as soon as, when) and the Main Clause.Using "will" or "shall" in both clauses is a "Double Future" error. Even though the condition refers to the future, the grammar requires the Simple Present to express it. 💢 Application to the Given Question - The word unless introduces a conditional clause. According to the rule, you cannot use "will" in a clause starting with "unless." Since the subject "the contractor" is singular, we must use the Simple Present verb submits. The main clause ("The project manager will not authorize") correctly uses the future tense, so the error lies solely in the conditional part. More Examples for Clarity -Example 1 ✅: If it rains, we will cancel the match. (Not: If it will rain)Example 2 ✅: Until the sun sets, we will not return home. (Not: Until the sun will set)Example 3 ✅: When she arrives, I will inform you. (Not: When she will arrive)

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: The archaeologists carefully excavated the site for months,
documented every minor artifact they discovered, and
finally submit their findings to the Ministry of Culture.
e: The Correct Ans is Option (C) Replace “submit” with “submitted”. 📌 Rule / Concept: Consistency of Tenses (Parallelism in Time) In a sentence describing a sequence of actions that occurred in the past, all the verbs must remain in the Past Tense (V2) to maintain a logical and consistent timeline. If the narrative starts in the past (e.g., excavated, documented), it must continue in the past unless there is a specific reason to change the time frame. Application to the Given Question "...excavated the site... documented every minor artifact... and finally submit their findings..." In this sentence, three distinct actions are performed by the archaeologists: They excavated (Past Tense - V2). They documented (Past Tense - V2). They submit (Present Tense - V1). Since the first two actions establish that the event happened in the past, the final action in the sequence must also be in the past tense to maintain parallelism. Therefore, "submit" is chronologically inconsistent. Corrected Sentence The archaeologists carefully excavated the site for months, documented every minor artifact they discovered, and finally submitted their findings to the Ministry of Culture.

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: Unless the candidates do not submit the requisite category certificates in the prescribed format,
their claims for reservation will not be considered at any stage of the recruitment process,
even if they produce supporting documents during the document verification round.
e:
The Correct Ans is Option (A).👉 Replace “do not submit” with “submit”.📌 Rule / Concept: “Unless” = If Not (No Double Negative)“Unless” already carries a negative meaning.
It means “if not.”Structure: Unless + Subject + Verb (affirmative form), main clauseWe must NOT use “not” in the clause introduced by “unless” because that creates a double negative.💢 Application to the Given Question - “Unless” already means “if not”. So the sentence actually becomes:If the candidates do not do not submit…This is grammatically incorrect.Correct structure: Unless the candidates submit the requisite category certificates…✅ More Examples for ClarityExample 1 ✅ - Unless you pay the fee, your registration will be cancelled.Example 2 ✅- Unless the bank verifies the documents, the loan will not be sanctioned.Example 3 ✅ - Unless the report is submitted on time, disciplinary action will follow.

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: The international regulatory body formally moved that the member nation, which had repeatedly violated
the trade agreement, is suspended from the assembly until it fully complies with the carbon emission
standards set during the last global environmental summit held in Paris.
e: The Correct Ans is Option (B). Replace “is” with “be”. 📌 Rule / Concept: The Mandative Subjunctive (Passive Voice) The Present Subjunctive mood is triggered by verbs of formal motion, demand, or requirement (such as move, demand, insist, mandate). When the action in the "that-clause" is passive (the subject is receiving the action), we must use the base form of the verb "to be" (be) followed by the past participle (V3). Even if the subject is singular (the member nation), the indicative forms "is," "am," or "are" are strictly prohibited in this mood. 💢 Application to the Given Question - The verb moved (in the sense of making a formal parliamentary motion or proposal) requires the subjunctive mood in the following clause. The member nation is the one being suspended (passive voice). Therefore, the indicative verb is must be replaced by the subjunctive base form be. More Examples for Clarity Example 1 ✅ The chairman moved that the meeting be adjourned. Example 2 ✅ It was proposed that the old building be demolished. Example 3 ✅ The advocate moved that the prisoner be released on bail.

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: final match of the tournament was
telecasted live to over fifty countries.
e: The Correct Ans is Option (C).Replace “telecasted” with “telecast”. 📌 Rule / Concept: Verbs with Identical Forms (The -cast Rule) –These verbs have same V1/V2/V3 :- Wed, Cost, Set, Bet, Bid, Thrust, Hit, Cut, Slit, Spread, Read, Burst, Quit, Shut, Shed, Rid, Cast, Telecast, Broadcast, Overcast, Forecast, etc. 💢 Application to the Given Question -This sentence is in the Passive Voice (was + V3). The word "telecasted" is used as the past participle. However, as per the rule, the V3 of telecast remains telecast. Therefore, the addition of the "-ed" suffix is incorrect and must be removed to maintain formal grammatical standards.

t: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
o: Every students must submit the assignment by Friday.
Every students must submits the assignment by Friday.
Every student must submit the assignment by Friday.
Every student must submits the assignment by Friday.
e: The sentence given in option (c) is grammatically correct. Options (a) and (b) are incorrect because the subject "students" is plural, but the determiner "every" requires a singular noun ("student") in place of the plural noun 'students'. The determiner "every" is used with a singular noun. Option (d) is also incorrect. After the modal verb "must", we use the base form of the verb. But 'submits' [third person singular verb] is not the base form. So, 'submits' should be replaced with the base form 'submit'. Option (b) also contains this error. Hence, (c) is the correct answer. The correct sentence is: Every student must submit the assignment by Friday. NOTE: Determiner: A modifying word that determines the kind of reference a noun or noun group has, for example, 'a', 'the', 'every', 'much', 'many', etc. Modal verb: A verb used with another verb to express an idea such as possibility that is not expressed by the main verb. The modal verbs in English are "can," "could," "may," "might," "must," "ought," "shall," "should," "will," and "would." They do not change their form (spelling) and they have no infinitive or participle (past/present). Example: I can speak Spanish. Here 'can' expresses the ability of the person to speak (main verb) Spanish. This ability cannot be expressed by the main verb 'speak'.

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: The first innings of the championship match were
significantly delayed due to an unexpected downpour
that left the outfield completely waterlogged.
e: The Correct Ans is Option (A). Replace “were” with “was”.Rule/Concept: Nouns Plural in Form but Singular in Meaning - Certain nouns in English end in -s and appear plural, but they represent a single unit or a single concept. When these nouns are used as the subject of a sentence, they must be followed by a singular verb.Application to the Given Question - The first innings of the championship match were significantly delayed...The word Innings is the same in both singular and plural forms. However, the use of the modifier "The first" clearly indicates that we are talking about one single unit of play. Therefore, the plural verb "were" is grammatically incorrect and must be replaced by the singular verb "was."Corrected Sentence - The first innings of the championship match was significantly delayed due to an unexpected downpour that left the outfield completely waterlogged.

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: Due to the integration of advanced neural networks, most
modern supercomputers now process highly complex
algorithms so fastly that users perceive absolutely no lag.
e: The Correct Ans is Option (C) Replace “fastly” with “fast”. Rule / Concept: Identical Adjective and Adverb Forms In English grammar, certain words are categorized as "flat adverbs" or words with identical forms. This means they function as both an adjective (modifying a noun) and an adverb (modifying a verb) without any change in spelling. The word "fast" is a primary example. Unlike "slow" which becomes "slowly," "fast" remains "fast" in both roles. These words have same adjective and adverb forms :- Fast, hard, late, straight, daily, weekly, monthly, yearly etc Application to the Given Question "...process highly complex algorithms so fastly that users perceive absolutely no lag." In this sentence, the word modifies the verb "process." Since it describes the manner of the action, an adverb is required. However, because "fast" is its own adverbial form, adding "-ly" creates a non-standard word. This is a classic "trap" question designed to see if a candidate blindly applies the "-ly" suffix rule to all adverbs. Corrected Sentence Due to the integration of advanced neural networks, most modern supercomputers now process highly complex algorithms so fast that users perceive absolutely no lag. More Examples for Clarity Example 1: He drove a fast car. (Adjective) ✅ Example 2: He drove the car very fast. (Adverb) ✅ Example 3: We need to make a fast decision. (Adjective) ✅ incorrect Usage Wrong example 1: The news spread fastly across the internet. ❌ Wrong example 2: A fastly moving object was spotted in the sky. ❌

t:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.
The board of directors was not entirely satisfied / with the vague explanations provided by the manager / and promptly demanded for a more comprehensive project status report.
o: The board of directors was not entirely satisfied
with the vague explanations provided by the manager
and promptly demanded for a more comprehensive project status report
e: The error is in part (d) with the preposition "for" after "demanded." The verb "demand" is a transitive verb that takes a direct object without a preposition when it means to ask for something forcefully. One "demands something," not "demands for something." The "for" is superfluous here. Correct Sentence: The board of directors was not entirely satisfied with the vague explanations provided by the manager and promptly demanded a more comprehensive project status report. Hence, option (d) is the correct answer. Note: · Transitive verb: Some verbs always need an object (a noun, phrase, or pronoun that refers to the person or thing that is affected by the action of the verb). These are called transitive verbs.

t:
Spot the erroneous part if any, in the following sentence.
The/ <u>deaf often has(A)/</u> a heightened sense of touch and visual perception/ <u>compared to(B)/</u> those/ <u>with normal hearing</u>. (C) / No error (D).
e:
Part A has an error. Certain adjectives (like poor, needy, aged, rich, dead etc.), when preceded by 'the' become nouns in plural form and require a plural verb if they are used as subjects. 'Deaf' is one such word, so 'has' [singular] will be replaced by 'have' [plural] to rectify the error in the sentence. Hence, (c) is the correct answer.
The final correct sentence would be: The deaf often have a heightened sense of touch and visual perception compared to those with normal hearing.

t:
Identify the segment in the sentence that contains a grammatical error. 
The two sisters, along with their brother, was excitedly planning a surprise birthday party for their parents, hoping to make it a memorable occasion.
o: The two sisters, along with their
brother, was excitedly planning a surprise
birthday party for their parents, hoping
to make it a memorable occasion
e: The phrase "along with their brother" is an additional descriptive element rather than a coordinating phrase like "as well as." Here, the compound subject "The two sisters, along with their brother" includes plural ("sisters") and singular ("brother") elements. When dealing with compound subjects like this, the verb typically agrees with the plurality of the entire compound subject. Since "sisters" is plural, the correct verb form should be plural to match ("were" (plural verb) instead of "was" (singular verb)). Hence, (b) is the correct answer. Note: A compound subject is a subject in a sentence that consists of two or more nouns, pronouns, or noun phrases joined by a coordinating conjunction (such as "and" or "or") that share the same verb. The corrected sentence: The two sisters, along with their brother, were excitedly planning a surprise birthday party for their parents, hoping to make it a memorable occasion.

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: By the time the global summit concludes
this Friday, the delegates will discuss
e: The correct answer is Option (B). Replace “will discuss” with “will have discussed”. 📌 Rule: The Future Perfect "Deadline" When a sentence uses the phrase "By the time" (or By then, By next week) referring to the future, it establishes a specific deadline. Any action that is expected to be completed before that future deadline must be written in the Future Perfect Tense (will + have + V3). Future perfect + ‘by the time’ + present indefinite 💢 Application to the Question In this sentence, we have a fixed point in the future: "This Friday" (when the summit concludes). The Deadline: The moment the summit concludes (V1 - concludes). The Action: The discussion of the climate accords. The Logic: The delegates won't start discussing the accords exactly when the summit ends; the discussion must be finished by that time. Because the discussion is an "action-to-be-completed" before the end of the summit, the Simple Future ("will discuss") is logically incorrect. It must be shifted to the Future Perfect ("will have discussed"). Corrected Sentence By the time the global summit concludes this Friday, the delegates will have discussed several key climate accords.

t:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
The security guard warned us / not to enter the building / and to wait outside / unless the manager arrives.
e: The error is in the choice of conjunction. 'Unless' is used to express a condition (if not). 'Until' is used to express a condition of time (up to the point in time). The sentence refers to a point in time (when the manager arrives), so 'until' should be used. Correct sentence: The security guard warned us not to enter the building and to wait outside until the manager arrives. So, there is an error in the part mentioned in option d). Hence, option (d) is the answer. Note: A conjunction (also called a connective) is a word such as and, because, but, for, if, or, when etc. Conjunctions are used to connect phrases, clauses, and sentences.

t:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.
Unless you do not work diligently / towards your ambitious career goals, / achieving significant success will be quite difficult.
o: achieving significant success will be quite difficult
Unless you do not work diligently
e: The error is in the part "Unless you do not work diligently". "Unless" is a subordinating conjunction that means "if...not" or "except if." It already implies a negative condition. Therefore, using another negative like "do not" after "unless" creates a double negative and makes the sentence illogical or redundant. The "do not" should be removed. Correct Sentence: Unless you work diligently towards your ambitious career goals, achieving significant success will be quite difficult. Hence, option (b) is the correct answer. Note: · Subordinating conjunctions: Subordinating conjunctions connect subordinate clauses (dependent clauses) to the main clause of a sentence. "Unless" is a subordinating conjunction. · Redundancy/Double Negative: The use of "do not" with "unless" is redundant because "unless" inherently carries a negative meaning.

t: Select the sentence that is grammatically incorrect.
o: One-half of the employees were granted an early leave due to the festival.
Three-fourths of the office furniture was replaced during the renovation last month.
Two-thirds of the architectural plan have been drafted by the senior designer.
One-third of the milk has been used to prepare the dessert for the guests.
e: The Correct Ans is - Option (C)- The error lies in the verb agreement with the singular noun "plan."Rule/Concept: Fraction & Proportion Agreement In sentences starting with a fraction or a word like "half," the verb does not look at the fraction. Instead, it "jumps" to the noun after the word "of".If the noun is Plural: Use a Plural Verb.If the noun is Singular or Uncountable: Use a Singular Verb.Logic Breakdown:(A) One-half of the employees were: This is Correct. The noun "employees" is plural, so the verb must be plural ("were"). This confirms that "One-half" takes a plural verb when the noun is plural.(B) Three-fourths of the furniture was: This is Correct. "Furniture" is an uncountable noun. Uncountable nouns always take a singular verb ("was"), no matter how large the fraction is.(C) Two-thirds of the architectural plan have: This is INCORRECT. The noun after "of" is "plan," which is singular. Therefore, the verb must be singular ("has").(D) One-third of the milk has: This is Correct. "Milk" is uncountable, so the singular verb "has" is required.

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: Having neglected by his primary caregivers
during his formative years, the boy struggled
e: The Correct Ans is Option (A) Replace “Having neglected” with “Having been neglected”. 📌 Rule / Concept: Passive Perfect Participle (Having + been + V3) The Perfect Participle (Having + V3) indicates an action completed before the main verb. However, if the subject of the sentence (in this case, "the boy") is the receiver of that action rather than the doer, we must use the Passive form: Having + been + V3. Using "Having neglected" (Active) would imply the boy neglected someone else, which contradicts the logic of the sentence where he suffered the consequences of being neglected. 💢 Application to the Given Question "Having neglected by his primary caregivers..." In this context, the "primary caregivers" are the ones performing the action of neglecting, and "the boy" is the recipient. Because the sentence structure starts with the participle phrase referring to the boy, it must be in the passive voice to show that the neglect happened to him. Corrected Sentence Having been neglected by his primary caregivers during his formative years, the boy struggled to form stable emotional attachments. More Examples for Clarity Example 1 ✅ Having been defeated in the first round, the team practiced harder for the next season. Example 2 ✅ Having been told the truth, she felt a sense of immense relief. Example 3 ✅ Having been repaired twice already, the old car finally broke down for good.

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: It was the dying king’s last wish, as recorded by the royal scribe,
that his youngest daughter, despite her lack of political experience,
succeeds him to the throne to maintain the stability of the empire.
e: The Correct Ans is Option (C). Replace “succeeds” with “succeed”. 📌 Rule / Concept: The Mandative Subjunctive (Wishes and Requirements) The Present Subjunctive mood is triggered by nouns and verbs expressing a wish, requirement, or command (such as wish, demand, requirement, recommendation, order). When followed by a "that-clause," the verb in that clause must be in its base form (the infinitive without "to"). This remains true regardless of whether the subject is singular (e.g., daughter) or plural, and it does not change based on the tense of the main sentence. 💢 Application to the Given Question - The noun wish (acting as the trigger) followed by the conjunction that sets the requirement for the subjunctive mood. Even though "youngest daughter" is a singular subject which would normally take the indicative verb "succeeds," the subjunctive rule mandates the base form succeed.

t:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
Engaging in a deep and contemplative process, she took the time to carefully think as the various possibilities, considering various perspectives and potential outcomes before arriving at a well-considered and thoughtful decision.
o: Engaging in a deep and contemplative process,
considering various perspectives and potential outcomes
before arriving at a well-considered and thoughtful decision.
she took the time to carefully think as the various possibilities,
e: Adverb 'as' cannot be used with- 'name, elect, think, consider, call, appoint, make, choose'. So, 'think as' will be changed to 'think about (give thought to)' in the given sentence. The correct sentence is- "Engaging in a deep and contemplative process, she took the time to carefully think about the various possibilities, considering various perspectives and potential outcomes before arriving at a well-considered and thoughtful decision." Hence, option (d) is correct.

t:
In the following question, a sentence is given which is divided into four parts. Out of the four parts, one part contains an error. Mark that option as your answer. 
Neither my sister(A)/ nor I thinks that David(B)/ could do such a(C)/ horrible thing as a murder(D).
e:
Part B has an error. If a compound subject is joined with the words 'either/or 'neither/nor), the verb must agree with the subject that is closer to the verb. 'I' is closer to the verb, so 'thinks' will be replaced by 'think'. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.
The final sentence would be: Neither my sister nor I think that David could do such a horrible thing as a murder.

t:
The following sentence has been split into three segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is error free, mark 'No error' as your answer.
More than one student (1)/ have attended the state level (2)/ quiz competition from my school./(3) No error (4)
e: The correct sentence is "More than one student has attended the state level quiz competition from my school". The noun and verb followed by 'more than one' will always be singular. More than one means not merely. The given sentence should be understood as 'not merely one student has attended the quiz competition (but many have)'. Hence, option (b) is the answer.

t:
In the given sentence, several segments have been underlined. One of these underlined segments is grammatically incorrect in the context of its usage in the sentence. Identify the incorrect segment from the following options. 
He would never <u>compromised his principles</u>, <u>even when faced with adversity</u>, <u>consistently upholding his integrity</u> and <u>staying true to his values</u>.
e: The verb "compromised" [past form verb] is incorrect because when "would" (modal verb) is used, the base form of the verb should follow. So, in this case, it should be "He would never compromise his principles" rather than "He would never compromised his principles." The correct structure is "would never" + the base form of the verb. Hence, (a) is the correct answer. The final correct sentence would be: He would never compromise his principles, even when faced with adversity, consistently upholding his integrity and staying true to his values. Note: Modal verb: A verb used with another verb to express an idea such as possibility that is not expressed by the main verb. The modal verbs in English are "can," "could," "may," "might," "must," "ought," "shall," "should," "will," and "would." They do not change their form (spelling) and they have no infinitive or participle (past/present). Example: I can speak Spanish. Here 'can' expresses the ability of the person to speak (main verb) Spanish. This ability cannot be expressed by the main verb 'speak'.

t:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.
Mani Kaul begun his career as an actor and a director of short films before doing his debut feature film, 'Uski Roti.'
o: begun his career as an actor
e: In the given sentence, the part 'begun his career as an actor' is erroneous. The verb 'begun' is in Past Participle form (V3) which requires an auxiliary verb (has/have) to support it. Moreover, the verb indicates that the action is done in the past which can be denoted by a verb in Past form (V2). The correct verb to be used is 'began' in place of 'begun'. Hence, the correct answer is option (b). Note: V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s). Auxiliary verb: A verb that gives grammatical information that is not given by the main verb of a sentence. It supports the main verb. Auxiliary verbs help to form the various tenses, moods, and voices of other verbs. The principal ones are be, do, and have. Example: She will sing a song tomorrow. Here, 'will' is the auxiliary verb that supports the main verb 'sing'.

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
e: The Correct Ans is Option (B). Replace “himself” with “oneself”.📌 Rule / Concept: Pronoun Consistency with "One"When the indefinite pronoun "One" is used as the subject of a sentence to refer to people in general, it must maintain consistency in its reflexive and possessive forms.-Subject: One-Object: One-Possessive: One's-Reflexive: OneselfIn formal English (especially SSC/Banking exams), you cannot switch from "One" to "he," "him," "his," or "himself" within the same logical context.Application to the Given Question - In this sentence, the subject is "One." Therefore, the reflexive pronoun used later in the sentence must correspond to "One." The word "himself" is the reflexive form of "He," which creates a pronoun-antecedent disagreement. To correct this, "himself" must be changed to "oneself."More Examples for Clarity - Example 1 : One should take care of one's health. ✅Example 2 : One must finish one's work on time. ✅Example 3 : It is difficult for one to keep oneself calm under pressure. ✅Incorrect Usage - Wrong example 1 : One should respect his elders. ❌Wrong example 2 : If one works hard, he will definitely succeed. ❌🧠 Things to Remember / Exam Tips-The Apostrophe Trap: Be careful with the possessive form. It is one's (with an apostrophe). SSC often gives "ones" (plural) to trick you.-The "He/She" Temptation: In casual speaking, we often switch to "him" or "his" for convenience, but the exam strictly follows the "One-One's-Oneself" chain.

t:
In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. 
A study by (A)/ Corbett Tiger Reserve authorities claims (B)/ that tigers, elephants and leopards have been (C)/ killing each other. (D)
e:
Part D has an error. 
'Each other' is used when we talk about two things. In the given sentence, we talk about more than two types of animals. So, 'one another' should be used here. 
Hence, option (a) is the correct answer. 
The correct sentence is: A study by Corbett Tiger Reserve authorities claims that tigers, elephants and leopards have been killing one another.

t:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.
He quietly walked into the bustling antique shop, / admired a few vintage items on display, / and then sits near the ornate fireplace to read his book.
o: admired a few vintage items on display,
and then sits near the ornate fireplace to read his book
He quietly walked into the bustling antique shop,
e: The error is in part (c) regarding verb tense consistency. The sentence describes a sequence of actions in the past: "walked" (V2) and "admired" (V2). To maintain tense consistency, the third verb "sits" (V5 - simple present) should also be in the simple past tense, which is "sat" (V2). Correct Sentence: He quietly walked into the bustling antique shop, admired a few vintage items on display, and then sat near the ornate fireplace to read his book. Hence, option (c) is the correct answer. Note: · Tense Consistency: In a sentence or paragraph, verbs should generally remain in the same tense unless there's a logical reason for a shift (e.g., describing events at different times). · V2 (Past form of verb): The form of the verb used to indicate an action that happened in the past. · V5 (Third person singular): The base form of the verb with -s or -es added, used for third-person singular subjects in the simple present tense.

t: The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.The captain of the ship, rather than the crew members who were rescued during the storm, ________ expected to testify before the maritime commission tomorrow morning.
e: The Correct Ans is - Option (C)-The blank should be filled with the singular verb "is".Rule/Concept: First Subject Priority When two subjects are joined by "rather than," the verb must agree strictly with the first subject. The phrase following "rather than" is a qualifier (extra information) and does not influence the number of the verb.Logic Breakdown:The Main Subject: The primary subject is "The captain" (Singular).The Qualifier: "rather than the crew members..." is a sub-qualifier. Even though "members" is plural, it is ignored for the main verb agreement.The Verb Selection (The Modal Trap): (B) should and (D) must are modal verbs. While they can be used with singular subjects, they do not require the word "be" immediately after them unless it's passive ("should be expected").Since the sentence uses "expected" (adjective/participle form) to describe a scheduled event, we need a linking verb.Correct Sentence: The captain of the ship, rather than the crew members who were rescued during the storm, is expected to testify before the maritime commission tomorrow morning.

t:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
Since Monday, I am trying to reach him but he is neither responding to my calls nor replying to my messages.
e: The error lies in option (b). 'Since' is a time expression that denotes a point of time. The rule is: Present Indefinite + Time expression= Present Perfect. For example: Monika has known me since 1995. Similarly, in this question, 'Since' is a time expression. So, 'am trying' must be replaced by 'have been trying' (present perfect tense) in the sentence. Thus, the error is in option (b) am trying. Therefore, the corrected form of the sentence is: Since Monday, I have been trying to reach him but he is neither responding to my calls nor replying to my messages. Additional Information: Another important Time expression is 'For'. 'Since' denotes a period of time. For example: Monika has known me for five months. ("five months" is a period of time)

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: Each of the senior researchers who were painstakingly
assigned to the multi-disciplinary international climate project
were asked to submit his findings by the end of the quarter
e: The Correct Ans is Option (C). Replace “were asked” with “was asked”Rule / Concept: Use of "Each" - The distributive pronoun "Each" is always considered a singular subject. When a sentence follows the structure "Each of + Plural Noun," the plural noun is simply part of a prepositional phrase. The verb must ignore that plural noun and agree with "Each."Analysis of the Complexity - This question is a "double-trap" because it contains two different verbs that look like they might be errors, but only one is.This is CORRECT. The word "who" refers back to "researchers" (plural). Therefore, the verb inside this specific clause must be plural.This is INCORRECT. This verb belongs to the subject "Each." Because "Each" is singular, the verb must be "was asked."Corrected Sentence - Each of the senior researchers who were painstakingly assigned to the multi-disciplinary international climate project was asked to submit his findings by the end of the quarter.Exam Tips for Long Sentences -

t:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. 
She smiled to/ the baby, who/ giggled in response, / at the play school.
e:
The verb "smile" is not typically followed by the preposition "to" when indicating the direction of the smile. Instead, "smile" is usually followed by the preposition "at" in such contexts. The correct phrase would be "She smiled at the baby". Thus, the error lies in segment (a), hence, (a) is the correct answer.
The corrected sentence: She smiled at the baby, who giggled in response, at the play school.

t:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
Navigating the labyrinthine corridors of / ancient history, historians unravels the complexities / of bygone civilizations, piecing together / narratives lost in the sands of time.
o: ancient history, historians unravels the complexities
narratives lost in the sands of time.
e:
The plural noun 'historians' needs to be followed by the plural verb 'unravel' or the past form verb 'unravelled' but not singular verb 'unravels'. Hence, option (b) is the answer. 
The correct sentence is: Navigating the labyrinthine corridors of ancient history, historians unravel the complexities of bygone civilizations, piecing together narratives lost in the sands of time.
OR
Navigating the labyrinthine corridors of ancient history, historians unravelled the complexities of bygone civilizations, piecing together narratives lost in the sands of time.

t:
The following sentence has been split into three segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is error free, mark 'No error' as your answer.
Aid workers have delivered vast quantities of food on the refugee camps.
e:
Option (c) has an error. The preposition used here in incorrect. 'On' should be replaced by 'to' as the latter is used to indicate a destination or direction. Hence, (c) is the correct answer.
'On' is used when the objects are physically in contact with or supported by a surface.

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: The cargo ship, carrying over five hundred containers of electronic goods and
industrial machinery, was bounded for the port of Rotterdam when it encountered
a severe tropical storm that forced the captain to alter the vessel’s original course.
e: The Correct Ans is Option (B). Replace “bounded” with “bound”.📌 Rule / Concept: Bound for vs. Bounded -These two words are often confused in competitive exams due to their similar appearance, but they serve entirely different functions:Bound for: This is an adjective phrase meaning "heading toward" or "destined for" a specific destination. It does not take an "-ed" suffix when used in this context (e.g., "The train is bound for Delhi").Bounded: This is the past tense of the verb bound, which means to leap or jump forward with great strides (e.g., "The deer bounded into the forest"). It can also mean to form a boundary (e.g., "The property is bounded by a fence").💢 Application to the Given Question - In this sentence, the context clearly refers to the destination of the cargo ship. Since the ship is "heading toward" Rotterdam, the correct adjective is bound. The word "bounded" would incorrectly imply that the ship was jumping or leaping toward the port.

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: Although the veteran diplomat was deeply disappointed by the collapse of
the peace talks, he ultimately resigned to the reality of the geopolitical
stalemate and returned to his home country for consultations.
e: The Correct Ans is Option (B).Replace “resigned to” with “resigned himself to”.📌 Rule / Concept: Reflexive Pronouns with the Verb 'Resign'The verb resign has two distinct meanings in English, and its grammatical structure changes accordingly:-To quit a job: In this sense, it is intransitive or takes a direct object (e.g., He resigned from the post). No reflexive pronoun is needed.-To accept something unpleasant: When resign means to reconcile oneself to a situation or to accept something inevitable, it is a transitive verb that must be followed by a reflexive pronoun (myself, himself, themselves, etc.) + the preposition to.Application to the Given Question - In this context, the diplomat is not "quitting" a job; he is "accepting" a disappointing reality. Therefore, the verb resign requires a reflexive pronoun that matches the subject "he." The correct phrase must be "resigned himself to."REMEMBER THE LIST:-Use reflexive pronoun after these verbs acquit, avail, reconcile, amuse, resign, avenge, exert, apply, adapt, adjust, pride, absent, enjoy etc.

t:
Select the grammatically correct sentence.

A. The childrens are playing in the park.
B. The child are playing in the park.
C. The childs are playing in the park.
D. The children are playing in the park.
e:
Sentence D is grammatically correct. There are no such words like 'childrens' and 'childs'. The word "children" is a plural noun, so it requires a plural verb form [are]. Also, 'child' is singular, so the plural verb 'are' cannot be used with it. Therefore, the correct sentence is "The children are playing in the park."
Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

t:
The following sentence has been split into three segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is error free, mark 'No error' as your answer.
If this solution is anhydrous, as it must be in any case for this purpose, / it does not act upon the metal of the compressors, / nor upon the iron bottles in which they are sent out.
o: If this solution is anhydrous, as it must be in any case for this purpose,
it does not act upon the metal of the compressors,
nor upon the iron bottles in which they are sent out
e: Here, the error is in the third part of the sentence. The use of the pronoun 'they' (plural) is incorrect as it refers to a singular subject 'this solution'. Use of 'it' (singular) in place of 'they' (plural) would have been correct and 'are' (plural verb) will be changed to 'is' (singular verb) accordingly. The correct sentence is: If this solution is anhydrous, as it must be in any case for this purpose, it does not act upon the metal of the compressors, nor upon the iron bottles in which it is sent out. Hence, (c) is correct.

t:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.
In 79 A.D., the Mount Vesuvius blew / its top, burying the ancient / cities of Pompeii and Herculaneum.
o: In 79 A.D., the Mount Vesuvius blew
e: We use the with the names of some mountains: the Matterhorn, the Jungfrau. We do not use the if the name includes Mount or Mountain: Mount Olympus, Brokeback Mountain. So, 'the' before 'Mount Vesuvius' needs to be removed in order to rectify the error. The correct sentence is: In 79 A.D., Mount Vesuvius blew its top, burying the ancient cities of Pompeii and Herculaneum. Hence, option (a) is the answer.

t:
In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option.
Ever since Justin made the (A)/ revelation, fans have been (B)/ impatiently waiting for him to (C)/ release the better version of the game. (D)
e:
Part D has an error. 
The article 'the' is used only before the superlative degree and not before the
positive or comparative degree. So, 'the better' should be replaced with 'a better' to rectify the given sentence. 
Hence, option (c) is the correct answer. 
The correct sentence is: Ever since Justin made the revelation, fans have been impatiently waiting for him to release a better version of the game.

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: After the sudden change in pressure, the pilot noticed that
one of the aircraft's external panels had come lose, necessitating
an unscheduled landing at the nearest airport for repairs.
e: The Correct Ans is Option (B). Replace “lose” with “loose”.📌 Rule / Concept: Confusing Words (Adjective vs. Verb)Loose (Adjective): This describes something that is not tight, detached, or not firmly fixed in place.Lose (Verb): This means to be deprived of something, to fail to win, or to misplace an item.In technical or mechanical contexts (like aircraft panels or screws), the adjective "loose" is required to describe the physical state of the object.💢 Application to the Given Question - In this sentence, the word is describing the state of the "external panel." The panel has become "unfastened" or "not firm." Therefore, the adjective loose must be used. Using the verb lose (which means to misplace) makes the sentence semantically incorrect, as the pilot did not "misplace" the panel, but rather noticed it was no longer secure.

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: Rohan has gone to the gym regularly
so he is very fit and capable of
e: The Correct Ans is Option (A) Replace “has gone” with “goes”.📌 Rule / Concept: Present Indefinite for Habitual Actions - Actions that are habitual, regular, or repeated are traditionally expressed using the Simple Present Tense (Present Indefinite). While the Present Perfect (has gone) can sometimes show a recently completed action, the presence of a frequency adverb like "regularly" or "daily" coupled with a present state of being ("so he is very fit") strongly dictates the use of the Simple Present to show a permanent routine. These adverbs of frequency represent habitual actions- Always, Often, Daily, Every day, Regularly, Frequently, Occasionally, Seldom, Never, etc. 💢 Application to the Given Question - In this context, the sentence describes Rohan's ongoing lifestyle choice that results in his current fitness. The auxiliary "has" + past participle "gone" implies a completed action or a specific experience, which contradicts the nature of a "regular" habit. To show a recurring routine, we must use the V1 form (with 's/es' for third-person singular).More Examples for Clarity - Example 1 - She always drinks tea in the morning before starting her work. ✅Example 2 - My father seldom watches television as he prefers reading journals. ✅Example 3 - They regularly visit the orphanage to distribute books and clothes. ✅Incorrect UsageWrong example 1 He is always coming late to the office every day. ❌ (Use: always comes)Wrong example 2 I have often seen the sunset from this balcony every evening. ❌ (Use: often see)

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: Our organization has consistently and will continue to provide
high-quality healthcare services to the underprivileged sections of society
as part of our long-term commitment to corporate social responsibility in this region.
e: The Correct Ans is Option (A). Replace “has consistently and will” with “has consistently provided and will”. 📌 Rule / Concept: Parallelism of Main Verbs with Different Auxiliaries - When two auxiliary verbs (like has, have, had, will, can, must) are used in a sentence and they require different forms of the main verb, the main verb must be explicitly mentioned for each auxiliary.Has/Have/Had requires the Past Participle (V3).Will/Shall/Can/May requires the Base Form (V1).If you use only one verb at the end, it must be grammatically compatible with both auxiliaries. If it isn't (e.g., has + provide is wrong), you must provide the correct form for each💢 Application to the Given Question - In this sentence, the auxiliary "has" needs a V3 (provided), while "will continue" is followed by an infinitive (to provide). By omitting the verb after "has," the sentence implies "has provide," which is grammatically incorrect. To be accurate, you must add the V3 form after "has." Corrected Sentence - Our organization has consistently provided and will continue to provide high-quality healthcare services to the underprivileged sections of society as part of our long-term commitment to corporate social responsibility in this region.

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: The mysterious disappearance of the confidential documents from the high-security vault
has roused deep suspicion among the federal investigators, who now believe
that an internal whistleblower might be involved in the sophisticated corporate espionage.
e: The Correct Ans is Option (B). Replace “roused” with “aroused”. 📌 Rule / Concept: Rouse vs. Arouse - While both verbs deal with "waking" or "stirring," they are used in distinct contexts:Rouse: Primarily refers to waking someone from sleep, unconsciousness, or physical inactivity. It is often used for a physical or literal awakening (e.g., "The alarm roused him from sleep").Arouse: Primarily refers to stimulating feelings, emotions, suspicions, or physiological responses. It deals with abstract concepts like curiosity, interest, or anger (e.g., "The news aroused his curiosity").💢 Application to the Given Question - In this sentence, the object is "suspicion," which is an emotion or a mental state. You do not physically wake suspicion from a nap; you stimulate or evoke it. Therefore, the abstract verb aroused is the grammatically correct choice here.More Examples for Clarity - Example 1: We managed to rouse the dog from its deep slumber. Example 2: The politician's controversial remarks aroused a great deal of anger.Example 3: It was difficult to rouse the troops after the exhausting march.

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: You will be surprised to know that
She hasn’t apologized for her rude
e: The Correct Ans is Option (C) Replace “nor her brother has” with “nor has her brother”. Rule / Concept: Partial Inversion after Negative Conjunctions When a sentence or a clause begins with a negative word or conjunction like Nor, Neither, Scarcely, Hardly, Seldom, or Never, we must use Inversion. Inversion means the Helping Verb (Auxiliary Verb) is placed before the Subject. Application to the Given Question The sentence contains two clauses. The second clause starts with the negative conjunction "nor": "...nor (Negative Conjunction) her brother (Subject) has (Helping Verb)..." According to the rule of inversion, since the clause starts with "nor," the helping verb "has" must jump in front of the subject "her brother." Corrected Sentence You will be surprised to know that she hasn’t apologized for her rude behaviour, nor has her brother. More Examples for Clarity Neither/Nor: He doesn't like tea, nor does he like coffee. (Not: nor he likes) Hardly: Hardly had I reached the station when the train left. (Not: Hardly I had) Seldom: Seldom do we see such a magnificent performance. (Not: Seldom we do)

t:
Identify the segment in the sentence that contains a grammatical error. 
I sent you the revised document, so please review it and revert back with any comments or questions by Friday.
o: I sent you the revised document,
e: The error is in segment (c) "revert back with any." The word "back" is redundant when used with "revert," as "revert" already means to return to a previous state or action. Therefore, the correct term to use in this context is simply "revert with any." Hence, (c) is the correct answer. The corrected sentence: I sent you the revised document, so please review it and revert with any comments or questions by Friday.

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: I know that I would study more
but I really don’t feel like
putting in the required effort right now.
e:
✅ Correct Choice is 👉 should. 

📌 Rule / Concept: Conditionality vs Modal Meaning (Zero / Implied Conditional)

This sentence does NOT contain a conditional structure, either explicit (if / unless / had / were) or implicit (a clearly recoverable condition).

Therefore:


 Any modal used here must stand independently, not depend on an unreal condition.


💢 Why “should” is correct - “Should” expresses:


 Duty 
 moral or logical obligation
 expected behaviour


In this sentence: “I know I should study more …”

The speaker is:


 aware of an obligation
 but admits a lack of motivation


This is a non-conditional, present-time statement.

No hypothetical situation is being constructed.

There is no conditional trigger such as:


 if I had more time
 if I were disciplined
 under different circumstances


Hence, should stands on its own and is grammatically complete.

t:
Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
<u>My cousin</u> <u>is working</u> as a software developer in <u>that multinational company</u> <u>since he graduated</u> from college two years ago.
e: The error is in the use of the Present Continuous tense in the segment is working. The sentence uses the conjunction 'since' to indicate a point in the past ('he graduated') from which an action has continued up to the present. For such actions that start in the past and continue to the present, the Present Perfect Continuous tense ('has been working') or the Present Perfect tense ('has worked') should be used. The Present Continuous tense ('is working') is typically used for actions happening right now or in the current period, but not with 'since' to denote duration from a past point. Correct sentence: My cousin has been working as a software developer in that multinational company since he graduated from college two years ago. Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: that he would always endeavour doing
his absolute best for his country.
e: The Correct Ans is Option (B) Replace “doing” with “to do”. 📌 Rule / Concept: Infinitives after Specific Verbs Verbs that are followed by infinitive:- Seem, appear, decide, desire, want, endeavor, stop, hurry, fail, happen, refuse, forget, remember, promise, prove etc. certain verbs are followed by an Infinitive (to + V1) to express a purpose, goal, or future action. The verb "Endeavour" (meaning to make an earnest effort) belongs to this group. When "endeavour" is used as the main verb, the action being attempted must be in the infinitive form. Using a Gerund (V{ing}) after these specific verbs is a common grammatical error. 💢 Application to the Given Question "...he would always endeavour doing his absolute best..." In this sentence, "endeavour" is the primary verb indicating the effort. The action he is trying to perform is "doing." According to the rules of verb patterns, "endeavour" cannot take the $-ing$ form directly. It must be paired with the infinitive "to do." Corrected Sentence The young diplomat solemnly promised that he would always endeavour to do his absolute best for his country. More Examples for Clarity Example 1 ✅ We must endeavour to protect our environment for future generations. Example 2 ✅ She refused to accept the bribe offered by the contractor. Example 3 ✅ They hope to reach the summit before sunset.

t:
The following sentence has been split into three segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is error free, mark 'No error' as your answer.
During the ride back to / River Heights, Emma sensed that Bill / was keeping something of her.
o: River Heights, Emma sensed that Bill
e: Option B is the right answer, as the correct preposition to be used here is 'from (her), not 'of (her)'. This phrase means to hide something from someone. Option D is eliminated. Options A and C are eliminated, as they contain no errors.

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: Do you recall to meet Arjun and his startup team
at the tech summit in Bengaluru last month, where
they were explaining their AI-based flood-prediction system?
e: The Correct Ans is Option (A) Replace “to meet” with “meeting”. 📌 Rule / Concept: Gerunds with Verbs of Memory (Recall) The verb "Recall" is part of a specific group of verbs (including recollect, deny, avoid, and suggest) that must be followed by a Gerund (V{ing}) when they refer to an action. In the context of memory, "Recall" specifically describes looking back at a completed event. Therefore, the action being remembered must be in the noun-form (V_{ing}) rather than the infinitive form (to + V1). 💢 Application to the Given Question "...Do you recall to meet Arjun and his startup team..." In this sentence, the context is clearly set in the past ("last month" at a "tech summit"). The speaker is asking the listener to search their memory for a completed action. Because the meeting has already occurred, the grammar requires the gerund "meeting". Using "to meet" is an error because the infinitive typically points toward an intended or future action, which contradicts the meaning of "recall." Corrected Sentence Do you recall meeting Arjun and his startup team at the tech summit in Bengaluru last month, where they were explaining their AI-based flood-prediction system? More Examples for Clarity Example 1 ✅ I don't recall seeing any suspicious activity near the building entrance last night. Example 2 ✅ The witness recollected hearing a loud bang before the lights went out. Example 3 ✅ She recalled visiting the Swiss Alps during her summer break in 2019.

t:
In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.
He says he is back to / work and is feeling much good / after keeping unwell for past few days.
o: work and is feeling much good
after keeping unwell for past few days
He says he is back to
e:
The adverb 'very' is used with a positive degree adjective while 'much' is used with a comparative degree adjective. For the given sentence, 'better' is a comparative degree of the adjective 'good'. So, the phrase 'much good' is incorrect. The correct phrase is either 'much better' or 'very good'.
Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.
The correct sentence is: He says he is back to work and is feeling much better after keeping unwell for past few days.

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: The local residents have terrified of the frequent
leopard sightings in the area since the beginning
of the monsoon season this year.
e: The Correct Ans is Option (A) Replace “have” with “have been”. 📌 Rule / Concept: use of passive verb form in the tense structure Use passive verb form structure when receiver is subject of the sentence. 💢 Application to the Given Question "...The local residents have terrified of the frequent leopard sightings..." In this sentence, "terrified" is an adjective describing the residents. If you say "have terrified," the sentence becomes active, meaning the residents scared someone else. To show that the residents are themselves in a state of terror since a point in the past (the monsoon), you must use "have been terrified. Corrected Sentence The local residents have been terrified of the frequent leopard sightings in the area since the beginning of the monsoon season this year.

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
e: The Correct Ans is Option (B) Replace “miserly” with “in a miserly manner”. Rule / Concept: Noun + ly (Adjectives) vs. Adverbs In English, most words ending in -ly are adverbs (formed from adjectives like quick/quickly). However, certain words ending in -ly are derived from nouns (Noun + ly) and function only as adjectives. Words like miserly, friendly, brotherly, fatherly, kingly, and cowardly cannot be used as adverbs. To use these as adverbs, we must use the phrase: "In a/an + Adjective + manner/way." Application to the Given Question "...he lived quite miserly in a small rented apartment." In this sentence, the word modifies the verb "lived." Therefore, we need an adverbial form. However, "miserly" is an adjective. You cannot "live miserly" any more than you can "live happy" (you must live happily). To fix this, we transform the adjective "miserly" into an adverbial phrase: "in a miserly manner." Corrected Sentence Although he was an aristocrat, he lived quite in a miserly manner in a small rented apartment. More Examples for Clarity Example 1: He is a friendly (Adj) person. ✅ Example 2: He behaved in a friendly manner (Adv phrase) with me. ✅ Example 3: It was a cowardly (Adj) act. ✅ Example 4: He fought in a cowardly manner. (Adv phrase) ✅ incorrect Usage Wrong example 1: He talked to me friendly. ❌ Wrong example 2: The soldier behaved cowardly in the battlefield. ❌ Things to Remember / Exam Tips The Suffix Trap: Do not assume every word ending in "-ly" is an adverb. The List: Memorize the common "Noun + ly" adjectives: Godly, Scholarly, Miserly, Niggardly, Orderly, Womanly.

t:
In the following question, a sentence is given which is divided into four parts. Out of the four parts, one part contains an error. Mark that option as your answer. 
Anna or her sisters (A)/ feeds the street dogs(B)/ every night after (C)/ their mother sleeps(D).
e:
Part B has an error. If a sentence contains a compound subject connected by 'or', the verb must agree with the subject nearer to it. The subject nearer to the verb is plural, so the verb should also be a plural. We need to replace 'feeds' by 'feed'. Hence, (d) is the correct answer. 
The final correct sentence would be: Anna or her sisters feed the street dogs every night after their mother sleeps.

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: Historical records indicate that the indigenous tribes of the valley
seldom if never migrated to the higher altitudes, preferring the fertile
plains that provided a steady supply of resources throughout the year.
e: The Correct Ans is Option (B) . Replace “seldom if never” with “seldom if ever”. Rule / Concept: Seldom if ever / Seldom or never Seldom is a negative adverb. To maintain logical and grammatical consistency, it must be paired correctly to form a compound adverbial phrase. There are only two standard idiomatic combinations: Seldom if ever: Meaning "rarely, if at all." Seldom or never: Meaning "rarely or not at all." Application to the Given Question ...seldom if never migrated to the higher altitudes... The sentence uses the hybrid phrase "seldom if never," which is a violation of the rule. Since the conjunction "if" is used, it must be followed by "ever" to suggest a possibility.
