Alternatively, the sentence could have used "seldom or never," but based on the structure provided, "if ever" is the standard correction for this specific error type More Examples for Clarity Example 1 : He seldom or never goes to the gym despite paying for a premium membership. ✅ Example 2 : Such a rare celestial event is seldom if ever seen twice in a single lifetime. ✅ Incorrect Usage Wrong example 1 : She seldom if never speaks in public meetings. ❌ Wrong example 2 : We seldom or ever visit our relatives in the countryside ❌ Things to Remember / Exam Tips The Trap: Examiners often swap the endings (seldom if never / seldom or ever) to confuse students who are reading too quickly. Always pause when you see "seldom" to check the conjunction-adverb pair.

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: The legendary cricketer walked off the field
and cheered by the massive crowd for his
e: The Correct Ans is Option (B). Replace “and cheered” with “and was cheered”. 📌 Rule / Concept: Passive Voice (Auxiliary Verb Necessity) - When the subject of a sentence is the receiver of an action rather than the performer, the sentence must be in the Passive Voice. The structure for Passive Voice in the Simple Past tense is: Subject + was/were + V3 (Past Participle).In a compound sentence where the subject performs one action (Active) but receives another (Passive), the auxiliary verb (was/were) must be explicitly mentioned for the passive part to maintain grammatical integrity.💢 Application to the Given Question - This sentence has two parts connected by "and":1. Active: The cricketer walked (He performed this action).2. Passive: The cricketer was cheered (The crowd performed the action on him).Without the word "was", the sentence implies the cricketer did the cheering himself ("The cricketer... cheered by the crowd" is logically and grammatically incomplete). To show that the crowd was the one giving the cheers, we must use the passive auxiliary verb "was".More Examples for Clarity - Example 1: The thief broke the window and was caught by the alarm system.Example 2: The student submitted the paper and was praised by the professor.

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: The diplomat noted that while there were several neighboring countries involved
in the water dispute, neither of them showed any willingness to
sign the bilateral agreement proposed by the international mediators.
e: The Correct Ans is Option (B). Replace “neither” with “none”.📌 Rule / Concept: Neither vs. None-Neither: Used specifically and strictly for exactly two persons or things.-None: Used for more than two (three or more) persons or things.Application to the Given Question - The sentence mentions "several" countries. In grammatical terms, "several" implies a number greater than two. Since the reference is to a group of more than two entities, using "neither" is grammatically incorrect. To refer to a negative choice among more than two options, "none" must be used.Incorrect Usage - Wrong example 1: Neither of the four brothers attended the wedding. ❌Wrong example 2: None of my parents could come to the meeting. ❌ (Logic: You have only two parents).

t:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
She has been working tirelessly since hours.
e:
'Since' is used to denote the point in time. But here, instead of a point in time, a period of time is mentioned for which we use the preposition 'for'. 
The correct sentence is: She has been working tirelessly for hours.
Hence, option (c) is the answer.

t:
Select the option that contains a grammatical error in the underlined portion. 
There are being installed various new computer's in the office of the head of the department of biochemistry.
o: There are being installed <u>various new computer's</u> in the office of the head of the department of biochemistry.
<u>There are being installed</u> various new computer's in the office of the head of the department of biochemistry.
There are being installed various new computer's <u>in the office of the head</u> of the department of biochemistry.
There are being installed various new computer's in the office of the head <u>of the department of biochemistry. </u>
e: Adding an apostrophe and an "s" to a word shows ownership, but it doesn't make a word plural. The sentence does not represent ownership/possession, but the plural form of 'computer'. So, "computer's" should be replaced with "computers" in order to rectify the error. The correct sentence is: There are being installed various new computers in the office of the head of the department of biochemistry. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

t:
The
following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the
segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: of a group of experienced professionals
with extensive knowledges in their fields
e: "Knowledges" should be replaced with "knowledge", as "knowledge" is an uncountable noun.

t: Select the sentence that is grammatically correct.
o: Neither Rutu nor her classmates is wanting to cancel the field trip.
Neither Rutu nor her classmates wants to cancel the field trip.
Neither her classmates nor Rutu wants to cancel the field trip.
Neither her classmates nor Rutu want to cancel the field trip.
e: The Correct Ans is - Option C: Neither her classmates nor Rutu wants to cancel the field trip. Rule/Concept: The Proximity Rule (Neither/Nor) In sentences using "neither... nor", the verb must agree with the subject that is physically closer to it in the sentence. The first subject mentioned has no effect on the verb form. Things to Remember/Exam Tips The "Nor" Anchor: Always draw a line after the word "nor." Everything before that line is irrelevant to the verb. Only look at the noun after the line. Don't "Balance" the Sentence: Many students think that if one subject is plural, the verb should be plural to "cover" everyone. This is a trap. Only the closest neighbour matters. The S-Rule: Remember that for most verbs in the present tense, adding an -s makes it singular (Rutu wants), while removing the -s makes it plural (Classmates want).

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: Inside the dark, damp cavern went they equipped
with only a single flashlight and a compass to
uncover the truth behind the local urban legend.
e: The Correct Ans is Option (A) Replace “went they” with “they went”. 📌 Rule / Concept: Inversion with Adverbs of Direction/place (Noun vs. Pronoun) When a sentence starts with an Adverb of Direction /place(Away, Down, Up, In, Out, etc.), the structure of the sentence depends entirely on whether the subject is a Noun or a Pronoun: If the subject is a NOUN: Full Inversion is required (Verb + Subject). If the subject is a PRONOUN: No Inversion is allowed (Subject + Verb). 💢 Application to the Given Question Inside the dark, damp cavern went they... In this sentence, the subject is "they", which is a personal pronoun. According to the rule, when the subject is a pronoun, we must use the normal word order (Subject + Verb). The inverted form "went they" is grammatically incorrect in this context. More Examples for Clarity Example 1 ✅: Away flew the bird. (Noun subject = Inversion) Example 2 ✅: Away it flew. (Pronoun subject = No Inversion) Example 3 ✅: Down fell the rain. (Noun subject = Inversion)

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
e: The Correct Ans is - Option (A). Replace “Raman’s friend’s tone” with “The tone of Raman’s friend”.Rule/Concept: Avoidance of Double Possessives - In formal English grammar, the use of two consecutive nouns in the possessive case (Double Apostrophe) is considered grammatically incorrect. It creates structural clumsiness. To fix this, we use the "of" construction for the first possession and an apostrophe for the second, or vice versa, to ensure there is only one 's in a single phrase.Application to the Given Question - In this sentence, the possession is layered: the tone belongs to the friend, and the friend belongs to Raman. Using two apostrophes ("Raman's" and "friend's") back-to-back violates the rule of double possessives. By restructuring it to "The tone of Raman's friend," we maintain the relationship while adhering to standard grammatical norms.Corrected Sentence - The tone of Raman’s friend was very rude and sarcastic during the entire duration of the meeting.More Examples:- Rohit’s brother’s car was stolen last night. ❌The car of Rohit’s brother was stolen last night. ✅Neha’s teacher’s advice helped me a lot. ❌The advice of Neha’s teacher helped me a lot. ✅

t:
Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
<u>The research team</u> <u>has submitted</u> <u>its detailed report about</u> the project's progress <u>to the management committee</u> last week.
e: The error is in the use of the Present Perfect tense in the segment "has submitted". The sentence contains the specific past time adverbial 'last week', which indicates that the action was completed at a definite time in the past. For actions completed at a specific past time, the Simple Past tense should be used. The correct verb form is 'submitted' (V2 form of submit). The Present Perfect tense ('has submitted') is used for actions that have a connection to the present or occurred at an unspecified time in the past. Correct sentence: The research team submitted its detailed report about the project's progress to the management committee last week. Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: The notorious gang of shoplifters vanished
from the shopping mall after the security
alarm was triggered by the infrared sensors.
e: The Correct Ans is Option (C). Replace “was triggered” with “had been triggered”. 📌 Rule / Concept: Sequence of Tenses (Past Perfect with "After") - When two actions occur in the past, one after another, the action that happened first must be in the Past Perfect Tense (had + V3). The second action (the result or later event) takes the Simple Past Tense (V2).When using "After", the structure is almost always:[Result: Simple Past] + after + [First Action: Past Perfect] 💢 Application to the Given Question - In this sentence, two things happened: the alarm went off, and the thieves vanished. Chronologically, the alarm had to go off first for the thieves to run away after it. Therefore, "was triggered" (Simple Past Passive) is incorrect because it treats both actions as happening at the same time or doesn't emphasize the sequence. To show the alarm was the "earlier" event, we must use the Past Perfect Passive: "had been triggered." More Examples for Clarity - Example 1 ✅: He went to sleep after he had finished his homework. (Homework first)Example 2 ✅: The guests left the party after they had eaten dinner. (Dinner first)Example 3 ✅: I bought the book after I had read the reviews. (Reviews first)

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: Being a staunch supporter of environmental
Sarah for the prestigious Green Award.
e: The Correct Ans is Option (A) Replace “Being a staunch supporter” with “As Sarah is a staunch supporter”. 📌 Rule / Concept: Fixing Dangling Participles in the First Part While most dangling participle errors are fixed by changing the subject after the comma (using passive voice), they can also be corrected in the first part by turning the participle phrase into a dependent clause. This involves adding a conjunction (like As, Because, Since) and a specific subject. This is often necessary when you want to keep the main clause in the active voice. 💢 Application to the Given Question Being a staunch supporter of environmental conservation, the local NGO nominated Sarah ...... As written, the "NGO" is being called a "staunch supporter." To fix this error in Part A without changing the structure of Part B and C, we must explicitly name the person the phrase refers to. By changing "Being..." to "As Sarah is...", we provide a clear subject for the attribute, thereby removing the grammatical ambiguity. Corrected Sentence As Sarah is a staunch supporter of environmental conservation, the local NGO nominated her for the prestigious Green Award. More Examples for Clarity Example 1 ✅: Since he was a destitute, Mr. Gupta gave him some money to buy food. (Corrects the original "Being a destitute" error in Part A). Example 2 ✅: Because the day was rainy, the school management decided to postpone the meet. (Corrects "Being a rainy day" in Part A). Example 3 ✅: As the room was dark, I could not find my keys. (Corrects "Being dark, I could not find my keys").

t:
In the sentence, identify the segment that contains the grammatical error.
Harassment and trolling are a major concern for women on social media platforms these days.
e:
When the nouns express a single idea and are placed together for emphasis, take a singular verb. In the given sentence, 'harassment and trolling' express a single idea. Replace 'Are' with 'Is' to make the sentence grammatically correct.
Hence, option (c) is the correct choice.

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: The meteorologist explained to the press
that the cyclonic storm is gaining momentum as it
moved closer to the coastal regions of Odisha.
e: The Correct Ans is Option (B). Replace “is gaining” with “was gaining”.📌 Rule / Concept: Sequence of Tenses (Indirect Speech)If the Principal Verb is in the Past Tense (e.g., said, explained, told, announced), the verb in the Subordinate Clause must also be in a Past Tense. 💢 Application to the Given Question - The reporting verb "explained" is in the Simple Past. Therefore, the subsequent action describing the storm must align with that past timeframe. Using "is gaining" (Present Continuous) creates a tense mismatch, as it implies a present action linked to a past explanation. To maintain symmetry with both "explained" and the later verb "moved," it must be changed to "was gaining."

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
e: Correction: Replace “brave Indians” with “the brave Indians”.Rule / Concept: People preceded by an Adjective – According to the notes provided, the definite article 'the' must be used with names of people or nationalities when they are preceded by an adjective. This structure identifies a specific group characterized by that quality.Corrected Sentence "During the colonial era, the brave Indians fought tirelessly against the oppressive foreign rule."More Examples for Clarity -1. The industrious Japanese are known for their technology.2. We should respect the ancient Greeks for their philosophy.Things to Remember / Exam TipsGeneral vs. Described: You can say "Indians are hardworking" (General), but if you add an adjective, you must add 'the' (e.g., "The hardworking Indians...").Adjective Position: Ensure the 'the' comes before the adjective, not between the adjective and the noun.

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: Despite the sudden transition to remote work,
the senior analysts are now used to
conduct their briefings via video calls.
e: The Correct Answer: Option (c). Correction: Replace "conduct" with "conducting". The Rule: "Be used to" + Gerund (V1+ ing)- When "used to" is preceded by a linking verb (such as is, am, are, was, were, get, or become), it functions as an adjective meaning "accustomed to" or "familiar with". In this specific structure, the word "to" acts as a preposition, not as part of an infinitive. According to the rules of grammar, a preposition must be followed by a Noun, Pronoun, or Gerund Application to the Sentence - Part (b) contains the linking verb "are" before the word "used". The sentence describes the analysts' current state of being familiar with or habituated to a new way of working (video conferencing). Because "are" is present, the verb following "to" must be in the gerund form (conducting). Why "conduct" is wrong: Using the base form ("conduct") would only be correct in the semi-modal structure "used to + V1” which describes a discontinued past habit (e.g., "They used to conduct briefings in person").

t:
Spot the erroneous part if any, in the following sentence.
The professor and/ <u>the researcher has(A)/</u> already/ <u>left the(B)/</u> conference/ <u>to attend an(C)/</u> important seminar. / No error (D).
e:
When two singular nouns are joined by 'and' and the definite article is placed before each noun, then that refers to different persons or things. This means the sentence has a plural subject. So, 'has' (singular verb) should be replaced by 'have' (plural verb) in the given sentence as the verb must agree with the subject. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.
The final correct sentence would be: The professor and the researcher have already left the conference to attend an important seminar.

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: So arrogantly he dismisses the valid concerns of his colleagues
that the entire department has become increasingly
reluctant to collaborate on any future research initiatives.
e: The Correct Ans is Option (A) Replace “he dismisses” with “does he dismiss”. 📌 Rule / Concept: Inversion with "So + Adverb" (Manner) When a sentence starts with "So + Adverb of Manner" (such as So rudely, So arrogantly, So beautifully), it is done to emphasize the manner in which an action is performed. In such cases, the sentence must follow the Partial Inversion structure. This means an auxiliary verb (do, does, did) must be placed before the subject. If the original sentence is in the Simple Present tense and the subject is singular (like he), we use "does" and change the main verb to its base form Application to the Given Question So arrogantly he dismisses the valid concerns... In this sentence, the phrase "So arrogantly" starts the sentence. The subject is "he" and the verb is "dismisses" (Simple Present). To apply inversion correctly, the auxiliary verb "does" must be placed before "he," and the verb "dismisses" must be changed to the base form "dismiss." Corrected Sentence So arrogantly does he dismiss the valid concerns of his colleagues that the entire department has become increasingly reluctant to collaborate on any future research initiatives. More Examples for Clarity Example 1 ✅: So sweetly did she sing that everyone was mesmerized. Example 2 ✅: So fluently does he speak French that people often mistake him for a local. Example 3 ✅: So bitterly did they argue that the neighbors had to call the police. 🧠 Things to Remember / Exam Tips The "That" Trigger: These sentences almost always follow the pattern: So + Adverb + Auxiliary + Subject + Main Verb... + THAT + Result. Verb Form: A very common trap in SSC Mains is using "does" but forgetting to remove the 's' from the main verb (e.g., So rudely does he behaves ❌). Always use the base form. Tense Harmony: Ensure the auxiliary verb matches the tense of the result clause. If the result is "wants" (present), use "does/do." If the result is "wanted" (past), use "did."

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: The investigative committee stated that neither of the two primary suspects
was able to provide a convincing alibi for their whereabouts
during the precise time the sophisticated cyber-heist occurred.
e: The Correct Ans is Option (B).Replace “their” with “his”.📌 Rule / Concept: Pronoun Agreement with Distributive Pronouns -Distributive pronouns such as Each, Either, and Neither refer to individuals within a group separately. Because they pick out members of a group "one at a time," they are grammatically singular. This means not only must the verb be singular, but any possessive pronoun referring back to the subject must also be singular (his, her, or its) rather than plural (their) [in that clause only.]Each/Either/Neither + of + Noun (plural) +Verb (singular) +Pro/Adj (Singular)Corrected Sentence - The investigative committee stated that neither of the two primary suspects was able to provide a convincing alibi for his whereabouts during the precise time the sophisticated cyber-heist occurred.Incorrect Usage - Wrong example 1: Each of the employees must sign their contract. ❌Wrong example 2: Neither of the players brought their kit to the field. ❌

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: In response to the recent surge in daring
breaks-in across the gated community, the local
police department has increased its nocturnal patrols.
e: The Correct Ans is Option (B).Replace “breaks-in” with “break-ins”Rule / Concept: Pluralizing Compound Nouns (Noun-Main vs. Phrasal Nouns)The rule for pluralizing compound nouns depends on how the compound is structured:-Noun + Preposition/Adverb (Noun is the Head): If there is a clear "principal" or "main" noun, you add the 's' to that noun.-Example: Passers-by, Runners-up, Mothers-in-law.-Verb + Preposition/Adverb (Phrasal Nouns): If the compound noun is formed from a phrasal verb and has no clear internal noun, the 's' is added at the very end.Example: Break-ins, Check-outs, Take-offs, Write-ups Application to the Given QuestionThe term "break-in" comes from the phrasal verb "to break in." In this compound form, "break" is not acting as a standalone noun being modified; rather, the entire phrase "break-in" functions as a single noun meaning a burglary. Therefore, to make it plural, the 's' must be placed at the end of the entire unit. "Breaks-in" is a common error made by over-applying the rule for words like "passers-by."Corrected Sentence - In response to the recent surge in daring break-ins across the gated community, the local police department has increased its nocturnal patrols.More Examples for Clarity -Example 1 - The pilot managed three successful take-offs during the training session.Example 2 - We observed several passers-by helping the stray dog. (Here, 'passer' is the main noun).Example 3 - There were multiple check-outs happening simultaneously at the hotel lobby.

t:
In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. 
We had no (A)/ other option left (B)/ but obeying (C)/ his command (D).
e:
Part C has an error. In a sentence, the adverb else is followed by 'but' and 'than' follows 'rather', 'other' and 'otherwise'. In this sentence, 'other' is incorrectly followed by 'but'.
The correct sentence is: We had no other option left than obeying his command.
Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
e: The Correct Ans is - Option (B). The plural possessive pronoun "their" must be replaced with the singular possessive pronoun "his" (or "his or her").Rule/Concept: Indefinite Pronouns are Singular Indefinite pronouns like Everybody, Everyone, Somebody, Someone, Nobody, No one, Each, and Every are always treated as singular subjects. Therefore, the pronouns and verbs that follow them must also be singular.Logic Breakdown:The Antecedent: The subject is "Everybody," which is grammatically singular.The Pronoun Error: Using "their" is a plural reference. In formal English exams, a singular antecedent must have a singular pronoun.The "Male Preference" Rule: Traditionally, in competitive exams, if the gender is not specified, we use the masculine singular pronoun "his" as the default.Agreement: "Everybody (Singular) ... his (Singular) work."Correct Sentence: Everybody should do his/her work honestly and diligently.

t: The following sentence has been split into three segments. Identify the segment that contains an error. If the sentence is free of any errors, mark 'No error' as your answer. The writer and director of the movie has/ put so many efforts to bring the cinematic narrative/ to life, delivering a compelling experience for audience.
o: the writer and director of the movie has
to life, delivering a compelling experience for audience
put so many efforts to bring the cinematic narrative
e:
The correct phrase is "put so much effort" rather than "put so many efforts." "Effort" is an uncountable noun in this context, so it should not be pluralized. Hence, (c) is the correct answer. 
The corrected sentence would be: The writer and director of the movie has put so much effort to bring the cinematic narrative to life, delivering a compelling experience for audience.

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: In light of the impending hurricane, the governor issued a mandatory
decree that every citizen residing in the low-lying coastal areas
evacuates their premises before the storm surge reaches the shoreline.
e: The Correct Ans is Option (C) - Replace “evacuates” with “evacuate”. 📌 Rule / Concept: The Mandative Subjunctive (Noun/Decree Triggers) The Present Subjunctive is used in "that-clauses" following nouns that express a formal command, decree, or necessity (such as decree, mandate, order, requirement, suggestion). In this mood, the verb in the following clause must be in its base form (the infinitive without "to"), regardless of whether the subject is singular or plural. 💢 Application to the Given Question - The noun decree acts as the trigger for the subjunctive mood. The subject of the "that-clause" is "every citizen," which is grammatically singular. In the indicative mood, "evacuates" would be correct; however, because a formal decree is being expressed, the subjunctive base form evacuate must be used. The length of the subject ("every citizen residing in the low-lying coastal areas") is designed to distract you from this rule.

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: In the interest of public safety and national security, it is absolutely vital that every high-ranking official
who has access to classified intelligence undergoes a rigorous background check
at least once every three years by an independent federal agency.
e: The Correct Ans is Option (B) - Replace “undergoes” with “undergo”. 📌 Rule / Concept: The Mandative Subjunctive (Adjective Triggers) The Present Subjunctive mood is not only triggered by verbs but also by specific adjectives that express necessity, urgency, or importance (such as vital, essential, imperative, important, mandatory). When these adjectives are followed by a "that-clause," the verb in that clause must remain in its base form, regardless of whether the subject is singular or plural. 💢 Application to the Given Question - The adjective vital functions as the trigger here. The subject of the following clause is "every high-ranking official." In standard indicative English, you would use "undergoes" (singular verb for a singular subject). However, because of the subjunctive trigger (vital), the verb must shift to its base form: undergo. More Examples for Clarity Example 1 ✅ It is vital that he be informed of the changes. Example 2 ✅ It is essential that the witness tell the truth. (Not tells) Example 3 ✅ It is important that she not forget the password. 🧠 Things to Remember / Exam Tips Spot the Adjective: Train your eyes to catch "It is [Adjective] that..." structures. Common culprits: Vital, Essential, Imperative, Crucial. The S-Ending Trap: This is the most effective way examiners hide errors in long sentences. They know "official undergoes" sounds natural to the untrained ear.

t:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
They all unanimously agrees and asserts that he excels in everything that he attempts.
e: In the given sentence, 'they' is a plural subject. According to subject-verb agreement, we should use a plural verb with a plural subject. The verbs 'agrees' and 'asserts' are singular verbs. So, they should be replaced with their plural forms 'agree' and 'assert' to rectify the given sentence. Therefore, the error is in the part in option (d). The correct sentence is: They all unanimously agree and assert that he excels in everything that he attempts. Hence, option (d) is the correct answer. Note: Subject-Verb Agreement: Matching up singular or plural subjects with singular or plural forms of a verb is part of the process called agreement. This can be understood better by the examples given: - "She likes cooking." [singular subject and verb] -- "They like to cook vegetables." [plural subject and verb]

t:
Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
<u>Policeman</u> came to <u>my village</u> and asked about <u>a person</u> who burgled <u>a house</u> last night.
e: The error is in the word "policeman," which is a singular noun without an article. In English, singular countable nouns typically require an article ("a," "an," or "the") unless they are proper nouns or used in a general sense. In this sentence, "Policeman" refers to a specific individual who came to the village, so it should be "The policeman" or "A policeman." The absence of an article makes the sentence grammatically incorrect. Thus, the option "policeman" contains the error. The correct sentence is-" A/The policeman came to my village and asked about a person who burgled a house last night."

t: Select the sentence that is grammatically correct.
o: In the culinary world, bread and butter are considered a classic and fundamental part of many traditional meals.
In the culinary world, bread and butter is considered a classic and fundamental part of many traditional meals.
In the culinary world, breads and butters are considered a classic and fundamental part of many traditional meals.
In the culinary world, bread and butter were considered a classic and fundamental part of many traditional meals.
e: This question tests subject-verb agreement for a compound subject that expresses a single, unified idea. When two nouns joined by "and" refer to a single concept or dish, they are treated as a singular subject. "Bread and butter" is a common pairing that is considered one item. · Subject: "bread and butter" (a single unit, hence singular). · Verb: Must be singular ("is"). Let's analyze the options: · a) This sentence incorrectly uses the plural verb "are." While there are two items, they function as one conceptual unit. · b) This sentence is grammatically correct. It treats "bread and butter" as a singular subject and uses the singular verb "is." · c) This sentence incorrectly pluralizes "breads" and "butters," which is unnatural in this context, and uses a plural verb. · d) This sentence incorrectly changes the tense to the past ("were"), altering the meaning from a general truth to a past fact. The correct sentence is: In the culinary world, bread and butter is considered a classic and fundamental part of many traditional meals. Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: Both the team captains, who had spent weeks preparing their presentations
have presented their strategies to the audience with confidence, illustrating his innovative ideas
showing meticulous planning and dedication that impressed the faculty members and peers alike.
e: The Correct Ans is Option (B)Replace "his" with "their".Rule / Concept: The subject both the team captains is plural, so the possessive pronoun referring back to it must also be plural. Using its (singular) creates a clear number mismatch.Corrected Sentence - Both the team captains, who had spent weeks preparing their presentations, have presented their strategies to the audience with confidence, illustrating their innovative ideas showing their meticulous planning and dedication that impressed the faculty members and peers alike.

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: At the prestigious art auction held
in London last night, the collector bidden
five million dollars for the portrait.
e: The Correct Ans is Option (B). Replace “bidden” with “bid”.Rule / Concept: Forms of the Verb 'Bid'The verb Bid is a classic trap because it follows two entirely different sets of inflections based on its meaning:Meaning: To offer a price (Auction/Tender)V1: Bid V2: Bid V3: BidMeaning: To wish, command, or say goodbye (Farewell/Order)V1: Bid V2: Bade V3: Bidden 💢 Application to the Given Question - In this sentence, the context is an auction (offering money for a portrait). When "bid" is used in the context of money or auctions, its Past Tense (V2) is simply bid. The word "bidden" is the Past Participle (V3) used only for commands or wishes (e.g., "He was bidden to come"). Using "bidden" in an auction context is a grammatical error.More Examples for Clarity - Example 1 ✅: He bid 10,000 rupees for the antique watch yesterday. (Auction – V2)Example 2 ✅: She bade him goodnight before leaving. (Wish - V2)Example 3 ✅: I have bidden him to stay away from trouble. (Command - V3)

t: The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar. In a courtroom where the evidence is overwhelmingly against the defendant, how _________ the defense attorney suggest that the eyewitnesses were intentionally misled by the prosecution?
e: The Correct Ans is Option (b). Rule/Concept: Interrogative Modal "Dare/Need"- In the interrogative structure (especially with Wh-words like How, Who, Why), "Dare/Need" can function as a modal verb. When it acts as a modal in a question: It comes before the subject. It is followed by the Bare Infinitive (V1 without "to"). It does not take 's' or 'es' regardless of whether the subject is singular or plural. Things to Remember / Exam Tips The Missing 'Does': If the sentence were "How does the attorney dare to suggest...", it would be a main verb construction. If 'does' is missing, it's a modal construction—so skip the 's' and the 'to'. Wh-Trigger: "How dare..." is a classic SSC/Banking phrase. Always look for V1 immediately after the subject in such cases. Tense Check: While "dared" can be used for the past, in the modal form, "dare" is used for both present and past in many contexts, but "dares" is always wrong in a modal structure.

t:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
These burrows need / to be wide dug / for the free / flow of water.
e: In the part mentioned in option (a), the verb 'dug' is incorrectly qualified by the adjective 'wide' instead of an adverb. The adverb 'widely' is to be used in the place of the adjective 'wide'. The correct sentence is: These burrows need to be widely dug for the free flow of water. Hence, the correct answer is option (a). Note: Qualifiers: A word or phrase that limits the meaning of another word or phrase or makes it less general. 'Adverbs' and 'adjectives' are qualifiers.

t:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
The famous author is known / not only for his brilliant novels / and also for his / insightful social commentary.
o: not only for his brilliant novels
e: The error is in the correlative conjunction pair. The phrase 'not only' must be followed by 'but also'. Using 'and also' is an incorrect pairing. This pair is used to add one more point or element to an existing one. Correct sentence: The famous author is known not only for his brilliant novels but also for his insightful social commentary. So, there is an error in the part mentioned in option c). Hence, option (c) is the answer. Note: Correlative Conjunctions are pairs of words that work together to connect two parts of a sentence that hold an equal value or correlate with one another. E.g., Either/Or, Neither/Nor, Not only/But also, etc.

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: ruins of Rome, a sudden thunderstorm
e: The Correct Ans is Option (A) Replace “While wandering” with “While the tourists were wandering”. 📌 Rule / Concept: Misrelated or Dangling Participles A participle is a verb acting as an adjective. When a sentence begins with a participle phrase (e.g., Walking..., Wandering..., Being...), the noun or pronoun immediately following the comma must be the logical doer of that action. If the subject following the comma cannot perform the action, the participle is "dangling" or "misrelated." 💢 Application to the Given Question While wandering through the ancient (A)/ ruins of Rome, a sudden (B)/ thunderstorm caught the tourists... (C) In this sentence, the subject following the comma is "a sudden thunderstorm." Grammatically, this implies that the thunderstorm was wandering through the ancient ruins. Since a thunderstorm cannot "wander," the participle is dangling. To fix this, we must provide a logical subject for the wandering (the tourists) within the first part. Corrected Sentence While the tourists were wandering through the ancient ruins of Rome, a sudden thunderstorm caught them off guard.

t: The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.Although he lacks the formal credentials of a scientist, his innovative approach to solving environmental issues proves that he is _________ Edison in his own right.
e: Rule / Concept: Proper Nouns used as Common Nouns- When a proper noun (the name of a specific person or place) is used as a common noun to represent a specific quality or to compare a person to a well-known figure, an indefinite article (A/An) or the definite article (The) is used before it. The choice between A and An depends entirely on the sound of the first letter of that proper noun.Application to the Given Question- "...his innovative approach to solving environmental issues proves that he is an Edison in his own right."Things to Remember / Exam Tips-1. The Comparison Logic: Using "A/An" suggests "a person possessing the qualities of." Using "The" suggests "the specific equivalent of."2. Sound Over Spelling: Never forget that this Rule is still subject to the vowel/consonant sound rule. For example, "a University" vs "an Honest man."More Examples for Clarity-1. He is a Newton of our class. (General comparison of intelligence)2. He is the Newton of this century. (Specific comparison)

t:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.
The government's new initiative to provide vocational training / aim to equip young people with practical skills, / thereby enhancing their employability in the competitive job market.
o: The government's new initiative to provide vocational training
thereby enhancing their employability in the competitive job market
aim to equip young people with practical skills,
e: The error is in the part "aim to equip young people with practical skills,". The subject of this clause is "The government's new initiative," which is singular. Therefore, the verb should be in its singular form. "Aim" (plural/base form) should be "aims" (singular). Correct Sentence: The government's new initiative to provide vocational training aims to equip young people with practical skills, thereby enhancing their employability in the competitive job market. Hence, option (d) is the correct answer. Note: · Subject-Verb Agreement: Matching up singular or plural subjects with singular or plural forms of a verb is part of the process called agreement. "Initiative" (singular subject) requires the singular verb "aims." · V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s): 'aims' is the V5 form of the verb 'aim'.

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: Even though the chief editor rarely handles the lifestyle section personally,
she edits a special commemorative edition these days to celebrate
the silver jubilee of the publication's founding anniversary.
e: The Correct Ans is Option (B) Replace “edits” with “is editing”. 📌 Rule / Concept: Temporary Actions vs. Habitual ActionsWe use the Simple Present Tense to denote habitual actions, permanent truths, or routines (often marked by keywords like usually, rarely, generally). However, when an action is temporary—happening "these days," "this week," or "currently"—even if it is not happening at the exact moment of speaking, we must use the Present Continuous Tense (is/am/are + V1+ing).Use present continuous tense with these words- At this time, At this moment, At present, Currently, These days, Right now etc. 💢 Application to the Given Question - The sentence establishes a contrast: her habitual behavior is that she "rarely handles" the section (Simple Present). However, the phrase "these days" signals a temporary departure from that habit. Therefore, the static "edits" must be changed to the progressive "is editing" to reflect this temporary ongoing project.Corrected Sentence - Even though the chief editor rarely handles the lifestyle section personally, she is editing a special commemorative edition these days to celebrate the silver jubilee of the publication's founding anniversary. More examples for clarity – ❌ Incorrect Sentence - Although the professor usually teaches medieval history, he teaches a special course on economic policy these days.✅ Correct Sentence - Although the professor usually teaches medieval history, he is teaching a special course on economic policy these days.❌ Incorrect Sentence- The company normally operates from its Mumbai headquarters, but it shifts most of its operations to Delhi currently.✅ Correct Sentence - The company normally operates from its Mumbai headquarters, but it is shifting most of its operations to Delhi currently.

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: Under no circumstances the security personnel are permitted
to allow unauthorized visitors into the high-security server room
without a valid biometric clearance and prior written authorization.
e: The Correct Ans is Option (A) Replace “the security personnel are” with “are the security personnel”. 📌 Rule / Concept: Inversion with Negative Adverbial Phrases When a sentence begins with a restrictive or negative adverbial phrase such as Under no circumstances, At no time, In no way, On no account, or On no condition, the sentence must follow the rule of Partial Inversion. This means the auxiliary verb (is, are, was, were, do, does, did, has, have, had, or modals like should/will) must be placed before the subject. 💢 Application to the Given Question Under no circumstances the security personnel are permitted... In the sentence above, the phrase "Under no circumstances" is a strong negative restriction placed at the beginning for emphasis. Therefore, the subject "the security personnel" cannot be followed by the verb "are". The auxiliary verb "are" must be moved before the subject to satisfy the inversion requirement. Corrected Sentence Under no circumstances are the security personnel permitted to allow unauthorized visitors into the high-security server room without a valid biometric clearance and prior written authorization. More Examples for Clarity Example 1 ✅: At no time did the suspect admit to being present at the crime scene. Example 2 ✅: On no account must you disclose the password to anyone, including bank officials. Example 3 ✅: In no way does this minor setback affect our long-term growth strategy.

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: The Chief Justice of the Supreme Court has recommended that every legal practitioner, regardless
of their seniority or specialized field, strictly observes the updated protocols regarding the digital filing
of documents to ensure transparency and expedite the judicial process in the upcoming term.
e: The Correct Ans is Option (B). Replace “observes” with “observe”. 📌 Rule / Concept: The Present Subjunctive Mood The Present Subjunctive is used in a that-clause that follows certain verbs conveying a sense of necessity, suggestion, or command (e.g., recommend, suggest, insist, demand, mandate, propose). In this mood, the verb must be in its base form (the infinitive without "to"), regardless of whether the subject is singular or plural. "It is used to show indirect suggestion, prayer, advice, request, demand, and necessity." 💢 Application to the Given Question - The verb recommended in the main clause triggers the subjunctive mood in the subordinate clause starting with "that." Although the subject "every legal practitioner" is singular and would normally take the indicative verb "observes," the subjunctive rule mandates the base form observe. The addition of the adverb "strictly" does not change this requirement. More Examples for Clarity Example 1 ✅ The committee recommended that he submit his resignation immediately. Example 2 ✅ It is recommended that a passenger arrive at the airport two hours early. Example 3 ✅ The doctor recommended that the patient be kept under observation.

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: Despite the heavy industrialization in the outskirts,
the natural sceneries of the countryside remain
largely untouched and pristine for the local tourists.
e: The Correct Ans is - Option (B). Replace “sceneries” with “scenery” and ‘remain’ with ‘remains.’Rule/Concept: Uncountable Nouns -Certain nouns in English are strictly uncountable and do not have a plural form. The word "Scenery" is an abstract noun that refers to the general appearance of a place. Because it is uncountable, it cannot be written as "sceneries" nor can it be used with plural verbs or numbers. It must always be treated as a singular entity.These nouns are used as singular noun:- Bread, Soap, Shampoo, Sand, Iron, Paper, Stone, Hair, Brick, Food, Grass, Garbage, Filth, Scenery, Machinery, Jewellery, Cutlery, Crockery, Stationery, Luggage, Baggage, Money, Evidence, Equipment, Advice, Work, Music, Information, Knowledge, Wealth, Business, Research, Abuse, Percentage, Alphabet etc.In the sentence provided, the word "sceneries" is used to describe the landscape of the countryside. Since "scenery" is an uncountable noun, the plural form "sceneries" is grammatically incorrect. Furthermore, as the subject becomes singular ("scenery"), the verb must also change from "remain" to "remains" to maintain subject-verb agreement.Corrected Sentence - Despite the heavy industrialization in the outskirts, the natural scenery of the countryside remains largely untouched and pristine for the local tourists.

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: The speaker of Lok Sabha emphasized
will and aspirations of the people of India.
e: Replace “Parliament” with “the Parliament”.Rule / Concept: Use of 'The' with Holy Books, Newspapers, and Statutory Bodies - The definite article 'the' is used before the names of holy books (e.g., the Geeta), newspapers (e.g., the Times of India), and statutory or constitutional bodies (e.g., the Parliament, the Judiciary).However, 'the' is not used before holy books when the author's name precedes them (e.g., Valmiki’s Ramayana).Corrected Sentence- The speaker of Lok Sabha emphasized that the Parliament represents the collective will and aspirations of the people of India.Things to Remember / Exam Tips- Just as we use 'the' for the press (The Hindu) and the wings of government (The Executive), always ensure these formal titles are treated as specific nouns.

t: The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar. Despite the biting cold of the Arctic expedition, the indigenous guides _________ trekking through chest-deep snow for several hours without a break.
e: Replace blank with “are used to”. Rule/Concept: Linking Verb + Used (Adjective) + To (Preposition) – In this structure, "used" functions as an adjective meaning "accustomed to" or "familiar with." It is preceded by a linking verb (is/am/are/was/were/get/become) and followed by the preposition "to". Because "to" is a preposition here, it must be followed by a Noun, Pronoun, or Gerund (V1+ing). Application to the Given Question - In question, the sentence describes a state of being familiar with a difficult activity. The word following the blank is "trekking" (a Gerund/V1+ing). Only the "be used to" structure can grammatically precede a gerund in this context. More Examples for Clarity - I am used to the loud noise of the city now. (Used to + Noun) She is used to working under immense pressure. (Used to + Gerund) Things to Remember / Exam Tips - The V1+ing Trigger: If you see a verb ending in -ing immediately after the blank, you almost certainly need a linking verb (is/am/are/was/were) before "used to." The "To" Nature: Remember that in "I used to go," 'to' is part of the infinitive. In "I am used to going," 'to' is a preposition. "Get" vs "Be": "Be used to" describes a state (already familiar), while "Get used to" describes the process (becoming familiar).

t:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
Ramayana is an ancient Sanskrit epic; it is believed to be written around 500 BC to 100 BC.
e:
"Ramayana" is an epic, so 'the' must be used before it.
The correct sentence would be "The Ramayana is an ancient Sanskrit epic; it is believed to have been written around 500 BC to 100 BC."

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: The aspiring actress reached the audition hall
much later than she planned because of the
unprecedented heavy traffic on the expressway.
e: The Correct Ans is Option (B) Replace “planned” with “had planned”. 📌 Rule / Concept: Past Perfect for the "Earlier Past" when we talk about two events that happened in the past, we must distinguish which one occurred first to maintain a logical timeline. The First Action (Earlier): Use Past Perfect (had + V3). The Second Action (Later): Use Simple Past (V2). Without the "had," the sentence implies both actions happened at the same time, which is logically impossible in this context—you must plan to arrive at a certain time before you actually reach (or fail to reach) the destination. 💢 Application to the Given Question "...reached the audition hall... much later than she planned..." There are two past actions here: She reached the hall (Action 2). She planned a specific arrival time (Action 1). Since the "planning" was finished long before she actually "reached" the hall, the verb "planned" must be in the Past Perfect. The sentence describes the failure to meet a pre-existing plan, making the planning the "past of the past." Corrected Sentence The aspiring actress reached the audition hall much later than she had planned because of the unprecedented heavy traffic on the expressway.

t:
In the question given below, three sentences are given which may or may not contain an error. Choose the one that is grammatically incorrect.
I. This watch is more expensive of the five watches he has been gifted.
II. Raghav, in my opinion, is humbler than loyal.
III. This watch is the more expensive of the two watches.
e:
Sentences I and II are incorrect. 
I: A comparative degree is used to compare two things. In the given sentence, the superlative degree should be used to talk about one of the five watches. 
The correct sentence is: This watch is the most expensive of the five watches he has been gifted.
II: When two qualities in the same person or thing are compared, the comparative
degree is formed by using more, instead of - r or - er with the positive. So, 'humbler' should be replaced with 'more humble'. 
The correct sentence is: Raghav, in my opinion, is more humble than loyal. 
III: When the selection of one of the two persons or things (sets of things) of the same kind is meant, the comparative degree is preceded by 'the' and is followed by 'of'. So, sentence III is correct. 
Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
e: The Correct Ans is - Option (C)- The plural verb "are" must be replaced with the singular verb "is."Rule/Concept: Subject vs. Subject Qualifier: The verb must always agree with the main subject, not the nouns found in the qualifying phrases (the sub-qualifiers). In this sentence, the verb should agree with "The quality," which is a singular uncountable noun.Logic Breakdown:The Main Subject: The sentence is not describing the mangoes themselves, but rather "The quality" of those mangoes.The Qualifier: "of the mangoes imported from the tropical islands" is a prepositional phrase acting as a qualifier. It provides extra detail but does not change the number of the subject.The Distractor: The word "islands" or "mangoes" is plural and sits right before the verb to trick the student into picking "are".Agreement: Since "Quality" is singular, the verb must be the singular form "is".Correct Sentence: The quality of the mangoes imported from the tropical islands is excellent.

t:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
While globalisation has been/ a boon, it also present challenges/ due to the heightened/ inter-dependency between countries.
o: a boon, it also present challenges
e: According to the subject verb agreement, 'it' is a singular pronoun so a singular verb must be used here, therefore the use of 'present' (third person plural verb) is incorrect, it must be replaced with 'presents' (third person singular). Hence, option (b) is correct. Note: Subject-Verb Agreement: Matching up singular or plural subjects with singular or plural forms of a verb is part of the process called agreement. This can be understood better by the examples given: - "She likes cooking." [singular subject and verb] -- "They like to cook vegetables." [plural subject and verb]

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: Beyond the jagged peaks of the Himalayan mountain range
was situated several ancient monasteries that had remained
untouched by modern civilization for over five centuries.
e: The Correct Ans is Option (B) Replace “was situated” with “were situated”. 📌 Rule / Concept: Full Inversion with Place Adverbials When a sentence begins with a Prepositional Phrase of Place (e.g., Beyond the hills, Under the tree, At the end of the street), and the verb is a verb of position or motion (e.g., be, stand, lie, sit, situated, located), Full Inversion occurs. In Full Inversion, the entire verb comes before the subject. Crucially, the verb must agree with the subject that follows it, not the noun in the prepositional phrase. 💢 Application to the Given Question ...was situated several ancient monasteries... In this sentence, the subject is "several ancient monasteries" (plural). The phrase at the beginning, "Beyond the jagged peaks of the Himalayan mountain range," is merely a place adverbial. Because the subject is plural, the verb must be "were situated" instead of the singular "was situated." Corrected Sentence Beyond the jagged peaks of the Himalayan mountain range were situated several ancient monasteries that had remained untouched by modern civilization for over five centuries. More Examples for Clarity Example 1 ✅: Under the table lies a sleeping cat. (Singular subject) Example 2 ✅: Among the trees were many colorful birds. (Plural subject) Example 3 ✅: At the top of the hill stands an old lighthouse. (Singular subject)

t: In the sentence below, identify the part of speech of the word “much”: The committee showed much interest in the proposal despite the financial risks associated with the project.
e: Answer: B) Adjective Explanation: An adjective is a word that describes or modifies a noun or pronoun. Here, “much” modifies the noun “interest.” much interest → tells us the quantity or degree of interest Since it describes the noun “interest,” “much” functions as an adjective.

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: knowledge are often prone to make
impulsive decisions during a market crash.
e: The Correct Ans is Option (B) Replace “prone to make” with “prone to making”. 📌 Rule / Concept: Use gerund or nouns after these phrases or adjectives Look forward to, With a view to, In addition to, Pay attention to, Conducive to, Accustomed to, Indifferent to, Object to Averse to, Opposed to Prone to, Vulnerable to, Addicted to, Devoted to, etc. 💢 Application to the Given Question The sentence uses the phrase "prone to," which describes a natural tendency or susceptibility. "...are often prone to make (Incorrect) impulsive decisions..." Because the "to" in "prone to" is a preposition, the verb "make" cannot stay in its base form. It must be converted into the gerund (noun form) "making." Corrected Sentence "Inexperienced investors who lack market knowledge are often prone to making impulsive decisions during a market crash." More Examples for Clarity Example 1: He is addicted to gambling. (Not addicted to gamble). Example 2: We are looking forward to meeting you. (Not look forward to meet). Example 3: He went to the library with a view to studying. (Not with a view to study).

t:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options.
Select the correct alternative.
The new almirah is <u>big</u> than this one.
e:
The comparative form of "big" is "bigger," used here to compare two almirahs.
More big: Incorrect, as "bigger" is the standard form.
Biggest: Superlative, used for more than two items.
More bigger: Redundant and incorrect.
The correct sentence: The new almirah is bigger than this one.
Hence, the correct answer is option (a)

t:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
Arush have been a member of the club since its inception.
e: The segment that contains a grammatical error is 'Arush have been'. The error is related to subject-verb agreement. "Arush" is a singular noun, so it should be followed by the singular verb "has," not the plural "have." Hence, (b) is the correct answer. The correct sentence is: Arush has been a member of the club since its inception. NOTE: Subject-verb agreement means that a subject and its verb must be both singular or plural: A singular subject takes a singular verb. A plural subject takes a plural verb. For example, in the sentence 'John lives in France', the subject John (singular 'he') 'agrees with' the third person singular form of the verb to live - lives.

t: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: William Shakespeare was a remarkable writer and a extraordinary
dramatist whose plays explore the complexities of human emotions
and the fragile nature of power and ambition.
e: Correction: Remove ‘a’ before “extraordinary”.Rule / Concept: Multiple Titles/Qualities for One Person – When two or more nouns or adjectives refer to the same person, the article is used only before the first description. Using an article before the second description would incorrectly imply that you are discussing two different individuals.Corrected Sentence - "William Shakespeare was a remarkable writer and extraordinary dramatist whose plays explore the complexities of human emotions."

t:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that has a grammatical error.
The thieves had no alternative / but to acquiesce with / the orders of / the police.
e:
The error lies in the segment "but to acquiesce with." The verb "acquiesce" is followed by the preposition "to" in standard English (e.g., "acquiesce to demands"), not "with." The correct segment should be "but to acquiesce to."
The correct sentence is: The thieves had no alternative but to acquiesce to the orders of the police.
Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

t:
The following sentence has been split into three segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is error free, mark 'No error' as your answer.
The company on Thursday clarified to staff / that there is no plans for company-wide layoffs / since it signed a deal to be acquired by the billionaire.
o: since it signed a deal to be acquired by the billionaire
that there is no plans for company-wide layoffs
The company on Thursday clarified to staff
e: The sentence talks about 'plans' (plural noun). Therefore, the phrase 'there is no plans' should be replaced with 'there are no plans' as the singular verb 'is' cannot be used with the plural noun 'plans'. Or the phrase 'there is no plan' can be used to rectify the error. Hence, option (b) is the correct answer. The correct sentence is: The company on Thursday clarified to staff that there are no plans for company-wide layoffs since it signed a deal to be acquired by the billionaire. OR The company on Thursday clarified to staff that there is no plan for company-wide layoffs since it signed a deal to be acquired by the billionaire.

t:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.
Even if a evidence was / relevant to the case, it couldn't / be used to determine the reprobate.
o: relevant to the case, it couldn't
be used to determine the reprobate.
e: 'Evidence' is an uncountable noun and indefinite article 'a' will not be used before it. Remove 'a' from the sentence in order to rectify the error. The correct sentence is: Even if evidence was relevant to the case, it couldn't be used to determine the reprobate. Hence, option (b) is the answer. Note: Countable and uncountable nouns: 1. Countable nouns are the class of nouns that can be counted, for example, 'table' - one table, two tables, three tables, etc. 2. Uncountable nouns are the nouns that cannot be counted or usually are not counted, for example, light, water, milk, information, furniture, etc. They do not generally have a plural form and can't be preceded by 'a' or 'an'. Many abstract nouns are typically uncountable. Some uncountable nouns can be used in the plural as well, depending on the meaning or context of the word. Definite and indefinite articles: In the English language, we have one definite article 'the'; it refers to or introduces, a particular, specific noun. 'An' and 'a' are indefinite articles; they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun.

t: The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar. In a society where corruption and greed often seem to dominate the headlines, it is heartening to observe that ultimately the honest _______ rewarded for their integrity.
e: The Correct Ans is - Option (A)- The blank should be filled with the plural verb "are". Rule/Concept: Adjectives Used as Nouns (The + Adjective) In English grammar, when the definite article "the" is placed before an adjective (like honest, poor, rich, blind, young, dead), the phrase functions as a plural noun. It refers to a whole group or class of people. Because it represents a group of individuals, it always takes a plural verb. Logic Breakdown: The Subject: "The honest" does not mean one honest person; it means "honest people in general." Why (C) is incorrect: "Is" is singular. While "honesty" (the abstract noun) takes a singular verb, "the honest" (the group of people) requires a plural verb. Correct Sentence: ...it is heartening to observe that ultimately the honest are rewarded for their integrity. Tips: The Group Rule: Always remember the formula: The + Adjective = Plural People. The poor are... (Poor people) The rich are... (Rich people) The unemployed are... (Unemployed people) Noun vs. Adjective: Do not confuse "The honest" with "Honesty." Honesty is the best policy. (Abstract noun = Singular) The honest are respected. (Group of people = Plural)

t: The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar. Given the presence of the suspect's fingerprints on the weapon and the lack of a plausible alibi, the jury concluded that the defendant _________ have been at the scene of the crime.
e: The Correct Ans is Option (c). Rule / Concept: Must (Logical Deduction / Strong Probability) – In English grammar, "Must" is used not only for obligation but also to express a strong logical conclusion or deduction based on available evidence. When we are almost 100% certain that something is true because of the facts, we use "must." When referring to the past, the structure used is Must + have + V3. Application to the Given Question – In this sentence, the "jury" is making a logical deduction based on two strong pieces of evidence: 1. The presence of fingerprints on the weapon, and 2. The lack of an alibi. These facts lead to a near-certain conclusion. Options like "should" (advice) or "can" (general ability) do not fit the context of a logical legal conclusion based on evidence. More Examples for Clarity - The ground is wet; it must have rained last night. (Deduction based on wet ground) ✔ He hasn't eaten all day; he must be starving. (Deduction based on hunger) ✔ Things to Remember / Exam Tips - Evidence-Based: If the sentence provides a "reason" or "fact" before the blank (like fingerprints, wet ground, etc.), look for Must to show the logical result. Must have + V3: This is the standard form for making deductions about the past. Must vs. May/Might: Use 'Must' for 90-100% certainty; use 'May/Might' for 30-50% uncertainty.

t: The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.Every one of the newly recruited management trainees from the prestigious institute ________ expected to submit ________ detailed research report on market trends by the end of this fiscal year.
e: The Correct Ans is - Option (D)- The blanks should be filled with the singular verb "is" and the singular possessive pronoun "his".Rule/Concept: Indefinite Pronoun Agreement Indefinite pronouns like "Every one," "Each," "Everyone," and "Nobody" are grammatically singular. They must be followed by a singular verb and a singular possessive pronoun, even if a plural noun (like trainees) comes in between as a qualifier.Logic Breakdown:The Main Subject: The subject is "Every one," which is singular. The phrase "of the newly recruited management trainees" is just a qualifier.Blank 1 (Verb): Since the subject is singular, we must use "is." This eliminates options (A) and (C).Blank 2 (Pronoun): This is where most students fail. Because the subject is "Every one," we must use the singular pronoun "his" (per standard exam convention) instead of the plural "their". This eliminates option (B).Agreement: "Every one (Singular) ... is (Singular) ... his (Singular)."Correct Sentence: Every one of the newly recruited management trainees from the prestigious institute is expected to submit his detailed research report on market trends by the end of this fiscal year.

t: The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar. Take the classified documents with you and keep them in the secure vault, lest the rival intelligence agencies _________ intercept the vital information during transit
e: The Correct Ans is Option (c). Rule/Concept: Lest... should (Fixed Conjunction Pair) – In English grammar, the conjunction "Lest" is used to express the idea of "to avoid the risk of" or "for fear that." It has a very specific grammatical requirement: it is almost always followed by the modal verb "should". Even though the sentence may imply a future possibility or a different modal sense (like may or might), "should" is the only grammatically correct companion for "lest" in formal exams. More Examples for Clarity - Walk carefully lest you should fall. He studied hard lest he should fail the examination. Things to Remember / Exam Tips - Lest Check: 90% of 'Should' questions in SSC revolve around the 'Lest...should' pair. Inversion Recognition: If a sentence starts with a blank and ends with a comma before a command/request, check if 'Should' (meaning 'If') fits. Probability: Use 'Should' when you are saying "I expect this to happen."

In the question given below, one part of the sentence may or may not have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. 
Measle is a highly contagious(A)/ virus that lives in the(B)/ nose and throat mucus(C)/ of an infected person(D).
e:
Part A has an error. There are certain nouns which apparently seem plural but are in fact singular. These include the names of some common diseases like mumps, rickets etc. 'Measles' is one such word. Hence, (a) is the correct answer. 
The correct sentence would be: Measles is a highly contagious virus that lives in the nose and throat mucus of an infected person.

t: The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar. During the annual cultural festival held at the university last year, every boy and every girl _______ present to witness the spectacular performance.
e: The Correct Ans is - Option (C)- The blank should be filled with the singular past tense verb "was". Rule 1: The "Each/Every" Rule (Subject-Verb Agreement) Even when multiple nouns are joined by "and," if they are preceded by "each" or "every," the entire subject is treated as singular. This is because the focus is on every individual person separately. Incorrect: Every boy and girl were... Correct: Every boy and girl was/is... Rule 2: Tense Consistency (Time Markers) In competitive exams, once you identify the subject is singular, you must check the time marker to choose between "is" and "was." The sentence contains the phrase "last year." "Last year" indicates a completed action in the past (Simple Past Tense). Therefore, the singular present verb "is" is incorrect, and the singular past verb "was" must be used. Correct Sentence: ...every boy and every girl was present to witness the spectacular performance.

t: In the sentence below, identify the part of speech of the word “well”: The diplomat spoke so well during the negotiations that even the opposing delegates acknowledged his remarkable clarity and confidence.
e: Answer: C) Adverb Explanation: An adverb is a word that modifies a verb, adjective, or another adverb. It often tells us how, when, where, or to what extent something happens. Here, “well” modifies the verb “spoke” and tells us how the diplomat spoke. spoke how? → well Therefore, “well” is an adverb.
